FCE is a voxel-based game.  That is where any similarities to that oft-compared "other highly popular voxel-based game" ends.  The point of FortressCraft is to build your base/machinery/infrastructure, and let it do the work for you.
You start out having crash-landed on a planet with with the most basic of machinery.  Your Central Power Hub to produce power, a research station to perform basic research, a smelter to smelt ore into bars, for use in the crafting station.  Selecting the easier resource difficulty levels will also give you a bonus coal deposit right near your CPH with the machinery needed to automate coal delivery right off the bat.
You then start finding resource deposits, placing extractors to mine from them, and collecting ore to smelt to then craft the machinery needed to automate that whole process.  As you discover different types of blocks, you can perform research to be able to craft new machinery to work faster or perform other tasks.  Once your basic research at the research station is all complete, you'll need to build a laboratory to continue higher levels of research.
Once you've got your infrastructure rolling along nicely, producing metal bars and power at a good rate, your base threat will increase to the point that the wasps start attacking.  Thus begins the tower defense aspect of the game.  You'll need to build a defense network to deal with the bugs.  And, of course, upgrade that network as your research and production levels increase, to deal with increasingly strong bugs.
The best part of this game, though, is the developer.  DjArcas is constantly adding new content into the game, and live streams development quite often.  A lot of game developers claim to be highly involved with their community.  And some even live up to that claim.  But Dj is the only one I know of that interacts with his community live on Twitch while he's writing the code for things that he's talking with the community about.  Many of the machines currently in the game are the result of suggestions made while he was streaming development.
If you like voxel-based games, city-building games, or strategy games, or any combination thereof, I highly recommend you check out FortressCraft Evolved.

Love this game! It's a awesome mix of voxel building, and survival through tower defense.  If you like to design and build large complex machines on a massive scale then you'll like this game.  If you like to manage those machines to get the most efficient designs, you'll like this game.
If you're really into tower defense, you might be a bit disappointed.  There are a good variety of enemies, but generally all you do is build A LOT of guns around your base.  The only strategy that comes into play is keeping them efficiently powered through your machines.
To win survival mode, you really need to think BIG.  Expect some of your structures to expand 1,000 blocks away from your starting base (although the majority will likely be within 500 blocks).   A general rule that worked for me is whenever I first build something, I make sure to leave space around it to build 4 or 5 more in the future because it seems like you always need more than you expect.  You'll feel like you have a lot of empty space around, but by mid game you'll be wondering where all that space went.
One complaint I've seen people bring up is that they get bored waiting for materials to be crafted.  If you're bored, you're doing it wrong.  This game is all about building big machines to automate production.  If you're sitting around waiting for research to complete - how about using that time to build more power generators to vastly improve research speed?  Don't have the materials to build more power?  Then go explore the world for new ore veins and build more machines to harvest it for you.  You have the tools and resources to build more mines and assembly lines to create more supplies than you know what to do with.
My only knock on the game is that a lot of information is missing from the in-game help.  If you want to learn many helpful tips that will take your base to the next level, expect to spend some time looking online or in the steam community pages for information.
The positive spin on this is that the developers are very active and are improving the game and adding new items/features on a near-daily basis so perhaps they haven't found the time to finish the help menu or aren't settled on the final stats of an item yet.

This game is designed similar to the MMO Würm.
To those that don't already know what Würm is, it is a ultra realistic medieval simulator with tons of grinding and real life day efforts to accomplish greater deeds, Minecraft copied Würm and made it into a piece of cake for newbies ( Arcade )
And today we have this game which is way more fast paced than Würm but also harder than Minecraft.
The concept so far is great and I expect lots of features/content to be added through the development periode of the next few months.
Pros:
-Great Medieval Simulation.
-Architectur / Terraforming is vital to be planned out ahead. ( No instant Minecraft houses )
-Cooperative play is highly recommended as resources is a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to collect on your own.
-Bandits/PVP players gets punished by lossing more stats on death.
-Great RPG elements shown through a very neat list of skill trees which unlocks upgrades along the paths you choose.
Cons:
-Animals are almost impossible to kill since a moose can take like 150 hits with a stone axe to kill and a wolf will straight up pwn you as you will not be propper quipped for combat until late game.
-Server crashing and slow server list made the game very frustrating, however a few days ago they patched some of bugs which have caused a relative stable version. ( I haven't crashed in awhile now )
-Combat got an animation but compared how they wanted to make it like Mount and Blade hit detection, it is just a prototype as of now and it is more like throwing a dice with a very low chance of hitting.
Conclusion:

Life is Feudal! This is the game of my dreams. Freedom to build, explore, craft, and work as a co-operative team in any way you wish.
It's really important to note that this is not a solo player game. I shudder to think of how long it would take to do anything by yourself, but it's got really great potential for co-operative play. Unfortunately, I've not had the experience of playing with others..my PC doesn't run the game well so I need it on a lower res, which pushes the chat UI off screen so I can only play with people I have on teamspeak or mumble. If you don't have a graphics card, I don't recommend this to you unless you can deal with really bad graphics, or are going to get a graphics card soon.
Negatives of this game that I struggle to overcome...it takes forever to do stuff. There's a lot of grinding for skills, and the time it takes to do certain things, or for crops/trees to grow don't always make sense. It takes half the time to erect a house as it does to uproot a tree stump. Fishing takes 30 seconds and you almost never catch anything. I guess this is stuff that will be ironed out in future updates, but if you can't deal with strange logics and bugs and unfinishedness then I wouldn't recommend this to you.
Positives...if you DO have a graphics card this game is gorgeous. Watching the sun go down over the lakes and mountains really is something to see. It's immersive, and exciting to see your settlement develop.
If you have a big bunch of friends, or friendly people on a server you frequent, it'll be great for you. You can get stuff done fast and I imagine it feels a lot more fulfilling than slogging over your tunnel for 4 hours with one other person.
In conclusion....it's a lot of money for an alpha but if you have the money to spare (and excessive amounts of time) then I'd definitely recommend it to you. It has a huge amount of potential for the future, which is really exciting!

First, you've got to understand this is an early alpha version of the game.  With that said, it's in a pretty advanced state and a lot of fun already. But here are a few key things to keep in mind:
- Some things are not yet implemented. Actually a lot of things, but there is still a ton to do in the game.
- This is not a quick action crafting/building game like Minecraft.  It takes hours (real time) to build a small mine looking for metal ores.  As you mine out a tunnel, you collect the rocks, you have to take those rocks and dump them somewhere or craft them into shaped stones (which are just as heavy as the rocks) so you must store them somewhere, then you can go back to mining.  It's a slow process...not for those who lack patience. For me it is relaxing, but your results may vary.
- In fact getting your skills up to the point where you can even mine takes a long time.  On the default settings, it takes hours of using your skills to raise them to the point where you learn new things.  The settings are customizable so each server can adjust them to speed things (even to the point of the rediculous).
- Single Player: There is essentially no single player (at least not in the normal PvE sense).  You can start a local server, make it private and no one else can join, then experiment all you want, but it will be a big lonely world.  I've split my time between experimenting on a solo local server and playing public servers.  Both are fun for me...
- Community: The server you join will make all the difference in terms of your enjoyment.  I've been servers where I was welcomed into a community, given a house, invited in to start working on my skills to be a productive member of that village.  And I've been on servers where people have been complete jerks.  There are hundreds of servers, find one that suits you.
TL;DR: If you're patient and looking for a slow paced, realistic game that is still in development, then this may be your game.  If you're looking for something with wall-to-wall action, keep looking, this ain't it.

One of the most beautiful, well-designed, well-executed platforming games to be ever made. And literally three games in one, each more in-depth and well-designed than the last. I was expecting "palette swap" or "alternate character" modes. No, Plague and Specter modes are redesigned from the ground up. Good on you if you were lucky to get this for $15.. but I would still recommend it even at $25.
I consider it a 9/10, but it's ultimately marred by the initial concept - slavish recreation of a platformer from the glory days. ♥♥♥♥♥♥ knockback, bottomless pits, forced scrolling segments (including the classic vertical scrolling "you need to know what to do ahead of time but you can't see over the top of the screen" type), cheap "ha ha we got you" deaths on environmental hazards, and a "you lose gold when you die but you can recover it" mechanic that inevitably will put the pickups where it's impossible for you to reach them.
Collectible hunting abounds, and any time you want to go back for something, you get to do the entire stage (including the boss) over again. Mega Man first implemented the "stage escape" in Mega Man X, which came out TWENTY YEARS before Shovel Knight's initial release. Too bad Yacht Club decided to base their game on NES platformers and not SNES ones.

I have now put a solid amount of time into the game and have a better grasp of exactly what Shadow Warrior 2 is.
Still a 10/10? YES.
Here's the thing, the story could be better. The side quest could have more diversity. But we have to take into account here that Flying Wild Hogs is not a triple A studio with unlimited funding, they have just over 100 people which is pretty small. Sure I could be a d and nip pick this game to death. There are flaws, but at the same time, I can see so many little details everywhere that these guys and gals put their heart and souls into. You can see their hardwork everywhere, from the weapons, artwork, modeling, levels and more. You can feel their love and passion, which is rare for a lot of games and more importantly, easily overlooked.
The positives far outweigh the negatives. The story and its side quest fall a little flat. Maybe it's something they can improve on in the future updates/dlc. Another thing is the confusing weapon customization system and crafting. Honestly, I think it's far better than Gearbox Software's but not as good as Blizzard's. They just need to tweak the upgrades menu to have filters so if we are looking for a specific bonus we can find it without scrolling for days and maybe buff some stats so we aren't all going for weapon dps/damage stats lol.
Crafting needs to be less randomized. If I slot 3 gems with Crit Damage, I'd expect the crafted item to have the most dominate trait of the 3 I placed to craft, which would be Crit, so the outcome has StatX+StatX+CritDamageX. Again, something that can be hashed out down the road and is far from game breaking. Let me point though on crafting that is overlooked. Sure taking 3 of your good gems in hopes to getting an epic version of them only to get a random duce sucks but the real diamond in the rough I found is crafting 3 white junk items repeatedly. Blues too! Cleans up my inventory and most importantly I got some seriously good legendary gems for 4K gold and 3 whites! So their crafting system does have benefits and is not a total waste as some say. Play around with it, just don't throw your best 3 in hoping to get a bombshell but instead take your junk gems and craft those, you'll have better results.
The gameplay is fluid, exciting, addicting and fun. I played both with the keyboard/mouse and my DS4 via SteamLink and was very satisfied with the controls. Another thing to note is the hit boxes are pretty damn good! I was skeptical but they nailed it and created a stellar FPS.They gave us some many ways to kill enemies it's unreal. The weapons are all diverse in their characteristics and are a lot of fun to swap around depending on your mood or lack of ammo lol. I love the mix of melee weapons and guns, they pulled it off very well. Gameplay wise, this game delivers and that's important. Some games are all about storytelling while games like this are about gameplay, it's not a bad thing and with our support we can expect better from both in the future. Personally, I love games like this where I can hop on and just destroy stuff without reason other than to destroy stuff. Great stress reliever!
The last thing I want to touch on is the levels. Yes, they are recycled and you don't feel like there is that many different stages. Again though, when you fully explore the levels, you can see a lot of love and care was put into their design, hidden areas and amazing detailed models from the trees, the Japanese style houses or even the weather. No one talks about the fact that you can literally destroy almost every object in the game, roughly 90% can be cut up or blown up. Best part is you can destroy a town, go off for a bit and come back and your destruction is still there. This game is so immersive, everything around you is so alive, movement everywhere, petals and pollen, bugs and birds, its this great mix of zen with chaos. A testiment to human existance really. I am hoping for more level diversity in the future as the procedural generated levels don't feel like more the 4-5 different levels to me but they all feel crafted and are so captivating and beautiful. Again, we can harp on these guys all day but they put love and care into this game and it shows everywhere. I see and I appreciate it.
I am very excited for the future of this game, this franchise and this awesome company. This game has flaws but I can see the love in it and so I forgive the misteps. I think with time they can further perfect it and honestly, it's not terrible or in need of desire overhaul, just needs some more trimming around the edges. Bottom line, they care about their fans, they care about their game and for that I commend them and support them. I am having a blast with this game despite the small hiccups, its a lot of fun. It scratches the right itch for me, I love Diablo 1 and Diablo 2 and am a big FPS guy, so I get the best of both with this game.
I am getting near 30, I have played a lot games and seen a lot of studios now. I can say this game is worth every penny and that this studio is on pace to be the next CDPR. They're Polish too, go figure! Lol I might be more critical if I paid triple A pricing but I didn't and like I said, there is so much attention to detail everywhere. The game is a work of art, everything is so beautiful, the weapons, the menu's, music, the levels. All of it. Very impressed and pleased with my purchase.
Highly recommend if you A. Like supporting good companies B. Like exciting FPS action C. Like customizing weapons/skills D. Amazing visuals

I picked up this game on sale because I had this craving to return to the cute little adventure games of my childhood. Call it nostalgia, whatever. I wasn't disappointed. This is a cute, short game and it's worth trying out.
Now, keep in mind, it IS a kids' game, and it's pretty simple because of that. I've tried to keep that in mind for this review. I can tell you this, I would absolutely recommend it for kids. I had a fun time with it as an adult, and I know this is the kind of thing I would have LOVED as a kid. Like, played it a gajillion times, loved. As an adult, one time is more than enough.
It's got a lot of fun minigames that teach about color, music, and artistic composition in an easy to learn way. It would be great enrichment and education for kids around elementary school age, and great for building creativity. The visuals are engaging and colorful, and the gameplay is simple and straightforward. It's short enough to sit down and play in one sitting, but not long enough to get boring at the end. The voice acting is a bit silly and not all that good, but it kind of just adds to the charm. My one real quip about it is that I would have liked a few more objects in the game to be interactive. Too many things LOOK like you could click on them but then you can't. And I'm pretty sure kid me would have been just as disappointed about that as adult me was. Probably even more, actually. Kid me would have wanted to click on ALL THE THINGS.
Bottom line? If you are a 20-something looking for a deep, engaging gaming experience that will rock your world, this is not it. But if you're looking for an excellent game for your kids to play, or if you just want to spend an evening playing something that hearkens back to the computer games you grew up on, then this is a great buy.

Was great, but it turned into a boring grindfest.
There was so much potential in this game, and I liked it for a while, but I can't really recommend it anymore.  It's changed into a money grab and you can tell that the passion has left this game in favor of "what shiney can I put in the game next."  This game heavily suffers from unpolished feature bloat simply for the sake of bringing in more cash.
For instance:
1. You have 1! biome, so forget exploring.  From the moment you step foot on the planet, you've seen everything it has to offer until you dig down for miles.
2. Grind for the sake of grind.  The equipment tiers are mostly just numeric advantages with color change, and very little functionality differences.  This is just to waste more of your time.
3. Huge vertical distances, just for the sake of it.  I'm not kidding, you can dig a very long way down before reaching the different levels, and this would be a feature if it weren't such a barren emptyness that you are digging through.  There's no point to the far distances other than to add to the transportation grind, and just to say "it's a huge world!"
4.  Dev prices things to fit his financial needs rather than to be competitive in the market.  The expansion has a price tag of 15 bucks, which is more than the original game!  A complete "screw you" to the loyal fans who bought the game originally.  Hell, I payed less for fallout 4 expansions than I would if I were to buy this one, and that's a AAA title!  Get real.
5. Monsters are an afterthought, with no real pathing, pathetic AI (because the dev can't be bothered) and a silly minigame based on your production levels.  There's no real threat at all to yourself except from falling damage.
All in all, these things make the game feel unpolished and the dev seems to have an obsession with gadgets and machines and cares little about gameplay.

This is the first part of a kinetic novel by the doujin group
. It was originally released in 2010, and they have continuations and other games by now as seen in their website. As a kinetic novel, it don't have choices (different from the sister genre visual novel).
Character art and story were done by
(
).
The script (code side and timings for every line, screen, image, sound) was writed originally in NScripter engine by
. While not open-sourced, royalty-free commercial use of NScripter is permitted and it's the same engine used by Tsukihime.
Almost all songs were composed by
.
As it should be obvious by the fanart in Shori pixiv and Jeffrey's handle in twitter as a melty blood player, they are both typemoon fans, and Wish is strongly influenced by tsukihime in artstyle, tropes and engine used originally. But the writing style and story itself can't be taked as derivated work from typemoon at all.
Backed by a
, Culture Select ported it to Unity engine, translated for both english and spanish and released it on Steam. While some things ended up slower (like the title screen menu), they have done a very nice job at translation and quality check. I didn't see a single typo from beggining to end. It's important to notice how crucial this change in engine is, as NScripter is only compatible with Windows.
As said before, art style of Shoori is strongly influenced by typemoon, is special Takeuchi older style. The background images beeing free sourced photos with filters to give a drawing/painting feel further reinforce the "tsukihime-roots" impression.
But the writing style is nothing like Kinoku Nasu. Intead of going for a more poetic and complex approach, the impression is that it overprioritize beeing direct, clean and consistent. The structure is not unlike "to Heart".
Specially in the first parts of the game, the scripting (timing of lines, images, sounds and effects likes screenshakes) in simply impecable, making it full obvious how much care there was for every single beat. As a consequence, the bigger parts (scenes, sequences, acts) flows very naturally.
Tokibu compostions (the majority beeing simple but beautifull piano songs in pentatonic) goes very well with both contemplative and action scenes.
Last things to be said: this is the 1st part of the history, so don't expect it to be conclusive. If you are ok with this, i would recomend it.

I am only part-way through the story, will update when I have finished, but so far:

The translation from Japanese (via a Kickstarter project) has gone very well, with the storyline being fantastic, very absorbing, and lengthy (the prologue took me 2 hours to read). The story makes uses of screen shaking, and background noises to help bring the atmosphere across. The storyline progresses by you pressing the return key for the sentence to keep it at your own pace of reading, or you can use the auto-read function, which you can set at differing speeds. Alternatively, pressing 'Ctrl' will fast-forward the text.
The background music changes depending on the area / scene, and really adds to the atmosphere. There are several different generic music pieces, as well as the special pieces for during fights, etc. The starting piece played during the introduction is brilliant.
The background graphics are all done as impressionist oil paintings, with the main characters depicted as normal sharp cartoon anime images. The text is a largish font, white with a black border, so is very legible on the dark and light backgrounds.
There are 100 save spots, so plenty. However, the story will only progress if it is the currently active window, so you cannot watch this in one window, and do something else in another window at the same time.

This game, at its core, is a point-and-click adventure mashed up with a stealth game, all wrapped up in pure pants-soiling nightmare fuel.  To get the full effect, I'd recommend playing it in the dark with a good pair of headphones.
The game follows Daniel as he wakes up in a creepy castle, not remembering anything.  He soon finds a note from himself urging him to find and kill Alexander.  Who is Alexander, and why does Daniel want him dead?  For that matter, who is Daniel and how did he wind up here with no memory?  Progressing through the game reveals the backstory bit by bit, which only serves to heighten the overall creepiness.
The puzzle aspect of the game isn't particularly challenging; most puzzles are of the find-the-widget variety with a few lever sequences and such thrown in.  The mouse controls can be somewhat peculiar at times, as well.  However, the puzzle-heavy areas tend to be well-lit and devoid of monsters, so you can take your time solving them.  And believe me, you'll be glad for the break.
The exploration-type areas are where the game really shines.  Your goal here is to either find the right widgets to complete the latest puzzle, or simply find the pasage to the next level.  However, these sections have little to no lighting, forcing you to make a choice: slink around in the dark, or expend your precious tinderboxes or lamp oil for illumination.  Staying in the dark causes your sanity to slowly drain away, but being in the light while monsters are about can be very bad for your health.
This game spares no effect in keeping the tension high.  There is the dark and gloomy setting, the constant offscreen sounds, the occasional jump-scares, the flashbacks... and that's when you're still in good shape.  Once your sanity starts to slip, good luck (to you, the player) trying to keep a level head.  And then there are the monsters.  Most of them can take you down in one or two hits, and just looking at them causes your sanity to take a hit as well as making it easier for them to spot you.  Whenever they show up, your options are pretty much run away or cower in the dark hoping that they go away before your sanity bottoms out.
So, if you like supernatural/sci-fi horror and enjoy being creeped out to the point where you hesitate to walk into a dark room even in your own house, this is the game for you.

Quite a solid RPG with some innovative concepts, but an engine that is really holding it back.
Pros:
- The story is good, the quests are varied and interesting and it rarely falls into the trap of "go [x] kill [#] of [y] and come back" quests.
- The lockpicking mechanic, while introduced poorly, is probably the best I've experienced in a game.
- Massive story campaign (I'm not even 1/3 of the way through it and I've played 25 hours thus far, though I am a "loot all the things" typpe fo player...).
- Magic system is quite unique and involved.
- The poison mechanic is pretty cool.
- The graphics have held up fairly well for a 3+ year old game.
- Overall an enjoyable experience that can be loosely compared to games like Skyrim, Neverwinter Nights or The Witcher (if you like those games, this is a game you should try.)
Cons:
- So many sacrifices made to keep this game on consoles.  The same button is jump, open, unlock and occationally counter in fights, the same button is run and sneak...  The game would have been much better as a PC only release (but I would say that about most RPGs...)
- Sneaking/assination skills are all but useless unless you're well over the level of the character you're trying to kill (even then, it's hit or miss).
- The enemies don't level with you, so it's easy to follow side quests into an area for which you are woefully unprepared, particularly early in the game.
- Once you have enough picked locks under your belt, 90% of the chests are locked with the highest level of lock possible, even in abandoned houses, as I said earlier, the lock-pick mechanic is excellent, but it gets tedious after a while.
- The walk/run/turn and general character handling can be frustrating at times and it makes it difficult to move around at times.
- Fall damage from pretty much any height.
It's a solid game, and if you do enjoy the Elder Scrolls, NWN and Witcher series it's worth playing (but please do not expect exactly those experiences.)  A better engine and fewer compromises for consoles would have drastically improved the output, but the experience is a solid one.

The name says it all.
UT2004 is an online shooter that was meant to show off the power of Unreal Engine 2.  It definitely accomplished its goal. If you don't want to play an online game, there's still Tournament and Instant Action modes (not to mention LAN).  The AI is great, there's a lot of diverse weapons, gamemodes, VEHICLES, and maps for you to play.
As for gameplay, for most of the time, it's like a Quake Live that doesn't suck.  There's no rocket jumping, sadly; there's plenty of physics/ragdolls, gibbing/messy shredding, and flicking off aliens to make up for it.  Just as a heads up, UT3 was pathetic compared to this.  More than that, play this one and its graphics will still be on par with other games (it just doesn't have HDR/Bloom, that's all).
Most of the time, you run around the map trying to take down as many enemies as you can while running from medkit to medkit.  The rest of the time, you use the Flak Cannon to maximize your trolling capacity and instantly win the game.
EDIT: The MP is still functional, as it turns out.  Epic shifted all of the UT games over to their own 3rd party servers.

As soon as I saw this game was unlocked on Steam, I had to buy it.
And I don't regret the decision one bit.
For those unaware, this is the sequel to Rosenkreuzstilette. A game that I recommended as well when it was put on Steam. I've played that game more then this one in the past. But now I do wish it was the other way around.
In this MegaMan-style game you take control of one of the bosses from the previous game, Freudia, instead of Spiritia. (Whom I will refer to as Tia from now on). This is one of the many improvements this game makes over the previous game. The reason for this is that Freudia does not have a traditional "Buster" weapon like Tia does. Instead she has a rapid-fire icicle weapon that has it's own weapon meter. This means you do not have to worry about charging it to do massive damage to an enemy.
Another positive is that when you beat a boss, Freudia doesn't just steal the bosses weapon. Instead she gains a new weapon that's inspired by the boss you just beat, but she gives it her own little unique twist. This adds even more of a breath of fresh air to the classic MegaMan style of gameplay.
Of course, as with all MegaMan style games, this game is indeed frustratingly difficult. You'll find yourself dying several times to a stage or boss until you finally get it down. And when you do, it's completely worth it.
Overall, the game does have it's ups and downs. However if you're a fan of MegaMan style platformers, cute anime girls, or both. Then pick this game up as soon as you can.

The first game was a love letter to Megaman 2. This game is more spread out in its references, and there are also quite a bit more of them, some of which you may like, others which might cause you to roll your eyes.
The change in character means that a lot of the level design is played slightly differently even if there are lots of similarities, as the Sting of Joy requires ammo where the spirit cannon did not. The difficulty also seems to be somewhat higher, but that might just be me not being used to it yet.
The sprite reuse isn't very appealing visually, but quite a bit bosswise is edited or changed, like if they had taken toadman and put him in megaman 5 right after 4, but with the attack patterns of someone else like gyroman.
Overall, I'd say its still very close to NES Megaman in presentation and gameplay, but is less 'safe' in how they designed things in many places. If you enjoyed the first one, you'll probably like this.
Side note seperate from gameplay, the translation seems to be not quite as good as the first game's, but its not like the story was anything big in the first place.

If you're a guy expecting a Triple A game then this is not for you.
If you liked OMSI and didn't mind the bugs, the lag and the horrible graphics then Fernbus is for you.
We are now in a world where people expect only 3 types of games; Triple A, Indie or♥♥♥♥♥♥game.
This is just like OMSI, it's not a Triple A, not an Indie and not a♥♥♥♥♥♥game. It's what used to be called a AA game.
It has bugs, the AI is far from perfect and the UI is bad.
Why aren't I bashing the game like the others are doing then?
Because of expectations. Life is Feudal, or what my friends and I have started to call it: Serf Simulator 2014, is a hardcore survival/build it all/kill the bad guy kind of game. It has been compared to Rust, DayZ, and Mount and Blade. To be honest, it does relate in different ways to all of these. You can build forever like Rust, the combat is very similar to Mount and Blade from what I have experienced so far, and you have to well...survive, like DayZ. Except no zombies.
Life is Feudal seperates itself heavily from these in that you have to do every little thing. This can be tedious, but in my opinion makes everything worth it once it's all done. Building a simple shack is so rewarding and makes you feel like you've made serious progress. That's only just the beginning though. There is a slew of skills to learn, buildings to construct, and players to make relations with....for the better or worse. Every character in the game is a player, which makes the world either very community-like or very dangerous.
You won't be able to do everything on your own. You must either find friends online, or invite your friends to join you. Characters have a skill cap and you must master certain skills to reach the furthest depths of that skill set. You'll need friends to provide resources from other skill trees to balance everything you work on.
Anyways, I've gone on long enough. I do love this game and absolutely cannot wait to see what the devs have in store for the MMO version of this. Oh, and to top everything off the game has only been out a couple of weeks and the devs have already released three patches. That's a good sign for the future.

*Very Early Alpha Build Reviewed, I will update as patches come out*
Update: A few patches have fixed up a lot of the issues with stability and (finally) added a proper server browser. A lot of skills/build trees remain broken at the moment by some odd choices in the order things were implemented, but if you're willing to have a generally fun (if simple) experience of "Rust with Swords", this is a decent buy.
LiF has an incredible amount of promise. For an early alpha build, I'd call the game nearly feature-complete. A great deal of the crafting is already in the game and ready to go. There's no lack of things to do right now, and the steady progression from shoeless caveman to hardscrabble dirt farmer comes at an engaging pace.
The main problem (and the reason I am not recommending it) is that while they have done a lot of work on the crafting system and modelling, even the most basic functionality of the game itself is missing. It's highly unstable, the game crashes frequently, and getting the game to load at all can be a challenge. At the moment, there are a number of quality of life features missing that make the game seem to actively resist being played. You cannot disconnect from servers, you must exit the game entirely to connect to another one, and the favorites/history tab does not work, meaning you can lose hours of work if you get disconnected (something that happens quite often) and are unable to find your server again.
It's interesting to see an early access title have the opposite problem that most have (big on features, low on basic functions), but I really can't recommend it at the moment. Future builds may improve stability and quality of life, but right now it's simply not worth the 40 dollars.

If you want something exciting to play after work (when you have limited time to invest in this game), then I would not recommend this game.
Good things:
Fun to play with friends - Terrorist Hunt, you can team up with your friends or some random people to play some missions against bots, this is the best thing about this game I have discovered, you can choose realistic mode, which really makes you to be careful, or you can choose normal if you want to finish up rather quickly.
Game itself is pretty good, fun to play.
Bad things:
Online Multiplayer - I hate it there, it is probably because I am a ''noob'', but I do not have that much time to invest in gaming and in this case I just think that this game is not for casual gamer. You can choose casual or ranked matchmaking, but it would not change the fact that most of the time you will end up dying, maybe will get 1-3 kills in 15-20 min game.
Online matchmaking - this kind of goes together with the first point I was making. The reason it is so hard to kill somebody is because usually you are matched with some pretty good players or hackers, idk (some people might just know how to disguise it very well), however, well above your rank & experience rating. I am Lvl 40, but usually get matched with players in their 100's. And it is no fun for me to die and wait while the matches end, it might be more interesting if we had more lives, but online multiplayer is always 5v5 (might be less if someone leaves) and it is always last team standing (they have these missions, but it almost never happens that someone completes the mission, one team just shoots out the other one 99% of the time).
Camping - this might be a good thing if you are into it, but not for me. Game is generally camping type, it is kind of slow, it is not your CoD MW type of game where you run and shoot, jump, hide, run & shoot again. This is more like, you camp for 1 or 2 minutes, then you decide to find another camping spot, and then someone just suddenly shoots you. Usually you move very slowly in this game either you are attacker or defender.
Conclusion
If you are looking for something fun, relaxing with limited time to invest - I do not recommend.
I would recommend if you are really into first person shooters, if you are looking for something tactical where you could really invest your time.

tl;dr It's tough recommending this game, but the bottom line I think I've got my money's worth and I think you probably will too.
Pros:
+ Great game concept.
Cons:
- Progression is broken. This game is about automation, but buildings' prerequisites and research requirements are set up so that you WILL spend hours grinding through things manually, and you WILL spend hours waiting on unavoidable bottlenecks. The game fights you every step of the way
- UI is broken. There's so much information that's not presented to the player (eg what research does), or presented in one of multiple places. There is a contextual help, but it really needs to be fleshed out to fill in huge gaps.
- Mobs are completely uninspired. Wasps will fly without stopping directly to the heart of your base, only attacking a single structure (the one that gets less and less important as the game progresses). There's no strategy to defense aside from supplying power to however many turrets it takes to kill the enemy.
- Low quality models and animations. Not super important considering the above points, but jerky conveyor belts sending items through each other, guns and enemies shooting globs of goo through walls, and everything else is just kind of distracting.
Those are some pretty massive cons for a game with only one pro, but I've got 38 hours in this game and only spent $8. Buy it and play it while watching TV or something. Or don't buy it and just play Factorio.

When you first start playing, the jerky camera work and non-intuitive movement/combat system might make you want to stop playing...you should follow that instinct.
After you get through the interface's learning curve, you stumble on to an actually decent action-RPG. Think Gothic but without interesting characters or a world that makes you care about. While I realize that's not a glowing recommendation, most of the game is actually enjoyable. The side-quests are interesting, and there are some genuinely funny moments. Unfortunately, you're never really *in* the game, because conversations are abysmal. The voice-acting is very poor, as are the conversation animations. You have to constantly refer to your journal for synopses, because the in-game dialogue is sometimes borderline nonsensical and leaves one wondering what actually just happened.
All that aside, it's perfectly possible to get tens of hours of solid gameplay out of this title...until you come to the final boss. I won't offer spoilers, but I will say that the mechanics of the final boss fight essentially toss aside all of the character building you've worked towards. The RPG elements die, only to be replaced by a clunky FPS/potion management test. Due to the game's refusal to let you save during the final battle, you will also be subjected to the final cutscreen each re-try (and there will be many, many re-tries if you actually want to win).
In other words, it starts out clunky, gets decent without ever being really good, and then ends with the least enjoyable boss fight I've ever encountered in a game.
I suppose the good news is that the characters are so unrelateable and uninteresting that I never felt compelled to power-through and beat the final boss, so on the positive side, at least you don't feel like you've lost too much if you never find out how the story ends.
If you have to play the game, just stop at the final boss and look online for a final cutscreen.

When I look at the negative reviews this game has received on Steam, either people have a problem starting the game, or they have played it no more than an hour before writing a negative review about this game. Very few of the negative reviews on this have been justifiably written, so I thought I should write my honest opinion of Fernbus Coach Simulator.
The Bus:
This game comes with two buses: the MAN Lions Coach and the Lions Coach C, which is slightly larger. Every little bit of the bus is detailed to real life; everything is clickable in the cockpit area, a bit like OMSI. What I hear quite a bit is that the tilt of the bus, when on the realistic setting, is anything but realistic. To anyone who thinks this - the developers asked real bus drivers to test the game and programmed the bus accordingly. Same goes for the engine - the devs recorded the noise of the bus from multiple locations and put it into the game. I've seen so many people complaining about the engine noise, when in fact it's quite realistic. Both buses, in my opinion, look and sound great. Definitely a highlight of this game.
The Map: TML Studios has really created something special with this game's world. Everything is very detailed (ex: random buildings next to autobahns, and tiny objects at building locations) and each city has character. You can tell the developers put their heart and soul into this map.
Graphics: When put on high or max, this game's graphics put SCS Software to shame. On low settings, this game looks comparable to OMSI or worse. It depends on what PC you have, but this game is pretty graphically demanding.
AI Traffic: AI traffic needs quite a bit of work. It's not terrible - cars stop behind you when you slow down, and they stop at traffic lights, but they really don't behave properly in many situations. When cars are stopped at traffic lights, they tend to jitter forward for a few seconds. It doesn't matter if you turn on your signal; cars will completely ignore your request as a bus driver. That being said, I haven't experienced any unfair crashes due to the AI crashing into me. So in conclusion, the AI needs work, but it's tolerable.
Passengers: The passengers actually look really nice in this game. They all look different and have individual names, and behave reasonably. This game also has, by far, the best check-in system of any simulator. Each person either has an online ticket, a paper ticket, or will ask you to buy a ticket on the spot. All of this occurs in real life, and it just feels great to check people in.
If you love buses (and Germany), this game is for you. If you want a simple game that you can jump into and play and enjoy, then you're probably going to find this game and difficult and painful to play. It's quite a complicated experience, and the tutorial doesn't tell you much. It takes a while to figure out how to operate the bus properly; it's not a very intuitive experience.
That being said, I believe this game is a great experience Maybe in a year or so, it will be an amazing game, with future patches, DLC and mod support coming soon. But for now, I'm perfectly fine playing what I have been given on August 25th.
UPDATE: Ok, this game has been out for almost a year now, and I still stand by everything i said above. However, the game has changed quite a lot since its release, and it's got two DLC packs as well, so here's a quick overview of what's changed and what's been improved:
- Better AI: The AI traffic has been updated several times since release, and now behaves much more reasonably than it did before. Vehicles no longer jitter forward upon stopping at a light; cars also generally go when the light is green now (they would frequently sit there and despawn before, which was quite irritating). In addition, there are more vehicles added now, including European heavy-haul trucks you see in ETS 2, as well as Flixbus AI vehicles on the road as well. You can also find buses at most depots now, which makes the bus stations feel a bit more alive and realistic.
- Better UI/Menus: The game's user interface has been completely remodeled from when it released, and is miles better than what it once was. Upon loading the game, you are treated to some nice pictures of in-game scenery, as well as some music playing in the background (some of the music really doesn't belong in a bus simulator). The Sat Nav on the bottom right corner has had information added to it, including your speed and the speed limit. The map will also zoom in and out, depending on the speed of your coach, to give you a better view of what's ahead, and you can adjust its zoom to show you more or less of the road.
- Better Performance: I never experienced any crashes when the game first came out, but the developers have nevertheless consistently improved the performance of this game, and it runs better now than it did before. It's still a graphically demanding game, and there are still peculiar parts of the map where the framerate will drop to abysmal levels, but overall the performance is pretty good.
- Better Sound/Effects: The motor noise of the MAN coaches has also been changed since the game came out, as well as tire noise effects to give you a sense that you're going fast. Sounds when traveling across a bridge or through a tunnel have been altered as well. There haven't been too many changes to the game's overall sound quality, but the changes that have been made are favorable.
These are by no means the only changes the developers have made to the game, but those are the ones that stick out in my mind the most. That's not to say this game is perfect, rather it is far from it. Pedestrians are still not roaming the cities. I didn't mention this in my original review, because the devs stated they would be putting pedestrians into the game eventually, but it's been nearly a year and there's still no sign of them. Passengers still don't walk onto the bus either, rather they teleport into the coach, and I've been waiting for them to fix this for quite a while now. Force feedback has not been implemented as well, although I do not use force feedback myself and, therefore, I am not raging like I've seen others do because of a lack of force feedback.
The AI and the performance could always be further improved, and I expect TML to continue to work on this game for the foreseeable future. When I first saw this game I was reminded of Robert E. Lee: Civil War General one and two, which I played an insane amount as a child. In reality, this game pales in comparison in almost every way.
This game has next to no content and very little replayability. This game is laughably overpriced.
Unit commands are reminiscent of the Total War series; however, they feel clunkier and worse in practice. Unlike the total war series, commands are often entirely ignored. At first glance it’s easy to chalk this inaccuracy up to communication issues or morale issues; however, after only an hour or two of gameplay it becomes clear that unit commands simply don’t work well. Rotating, falling back, and “holding” are particularly buggy.
Troops will often just wander off a few hundred yards in a direction, sometimes not even in the direction they are facing. “Hold” will not prevent this behavior. This makes defending a fortified position such as cemetery ridge, Culp’s Hill, etc a nightmare since you spend all of your time micromanaging your troops so they don’t wander off away from fortifications to go frolic in the open fields before being cut down by enemy gunfire. Again, at first I was willing to chalk some of this up to the breakdown of communications, humar error, glory hounds, etc; however, after a bit more time with the game it becomes obvious it's just a bug. It doesn't make sense for troops that are actively engaged in fire to consistently leave their fortified position behind a wall to walk willy nilly into an open field to be massacred.
Troops don’t alter their lines to actively take advantage of cover. If a wall isn’t perfectly straight then the units won’t use it effectively, lowering the unit’s overall cover rating.
Cannons don’t work well at all and will often refuse to fire regardless of visibility, line of sight, etc. The largest problem seems to be that if any friendly unit is even remotely near your cannons then they will refuse to fire. The computer solves this problem by putting cannons in front of, on the flanks of, or far behind their lines. This weird positioning often means a single unit can take out 3 or 4 units of artillery usually unopposed, which brings me to my next point.
The computer doesn’t seem to really react to your actions. You’re often allowed to move and position your units on their flanks and start wreaking havoc for a few minutes before the computer even begins to react.
The game lacks the ability to get detailed statistics about the ground you’re defending so it’s often impossible to tell important characteristics of terrain such as height, roughness, cover, etc. Determining where to move your units for visibility is a crapshoot, and particularly frustrating when dealing with cannons.
The “tutorial” (if we’re being kind enough to even call it that) is mediocre given its length and lack of integration into the game.
Minor: Units that are under fire have their unit numbers fall slowly while in combat. This makes sense for two units actively engaged; however, it does not make sense when being shot at by cannons or when massing fire all at once. This makes the game and certain tactics lack the “bite” they would truly have. It also sometimes feels like it has incorrect gameplay effects. Multiple cannons firing canister shot on bunched up enemy units should cause an immediate, drastic drop in men and morale, likely causing a rout. In this game both slowly trickle down and battle continues on merrily as if nothing happened.
All in all, my time would have been better spent playing one of the original Robert E. Lee: Civil War General games which have excellent campaigns, historical battles, better persistence between battles, better decisions, and better gameplay. Alternatively, if retro games aren’t your style then I’d recommend picking up Total War: Shogun 2, Total War: Shogun 2: Fall of the Samurai, Napoleon: Total War, or Empire: Total War.

Superb little game covering the entirety of the Gettysburg campaign at Battalion level. Immensely enjoyable, it captures the feel of large-scale ACW warfare perfectly, awarding strong tactical play. Battalions and supporting units (artillery, skirmishers) act in concert. Tactics involve the use of maneuver and terrain to overcome an opponent, making the game quite challenging if fighting an aggressive AI.
Campaign is broken into days, with surviving forces carrying over into the next day in the same location on the map captured in the previous days' battle. Reinforcements play a crucial role, and arrive at historical times during the campaign. Game starts out as a small (though challenging and at times chaotic) skirmish, eventually evolving into a massed pitch battle. AI is highly scaleable to suit any desired play style.
Game-Labs has put out a classic game of the genre here, don't be put off by its tablet roots. For the price a must buy for any PC grognard.

Tom Clancy's rainbow six siege is one of the most diverse and innovative tactical shooters I've ever played, the developers have clearly put their time and effort into this game, six siege is far from just another generic tactical shooter, the idea of this game is original and that's what sets it apart from other FPS shooters and six siege has definitely earned its place in one of the most played games on steam. To describe how good this game is in a few words is impossible, and because of that I'm gonna bring up points of why six siege is worth your money.
-Gameplay: Six siege as mentioned before is a very original game, you can play many different operators with many different gadgets that can be used to suit your team's needs, you can play from an extremely fast operator who carries a rocket launcher to breach walls or a human tank who carries a completely bullet/explosive proof extendable riot shield, to top it all off you can change your playstyles by switching the weapons of your operator.
-Graphics/Optimization: Six siege is a very optimized game for its size, you don't need a high-end PC to run it but you can't run it on a potato either, I run the game on High and still get a solid 120 FPS.
-Guns: Something that some people might want to know is the "feel" of the weapons in-game, for those of you who don't know its how realistic or proper a weapon is portrayed in game, if the weapon has a clunky animation or sound it just doesn't feel right using the weapon however, guns in six siege has a very good feel to them, from the sounds to the animations to the diverse customization you can have for them, the guns in this game are extremely satisfying use.
-Community: Like any other community no game community is perfect, including this one although it's safe to say that the general community is quite peaceful and if you are unlucky and encounter a common trashtalker just mute them. Most of the time players on your team can be toxic towards you if you're playing terribly and you don't seem to know what you're doing, most players find this irritating but this isn't that much of a big deal, if you plan on buying this game I urge you to finish the situations first before joining a casual game, situations will give you basic instructions to how to game is played, it doesn't take long and rewards you with XP and a ton of renown provided that you complete all objectives, playing a couple matches of terrorist hunt is also handy to get to know map layouts, breaching points and hard angles you can use to your advantage.
If you're bored of most of the shooters on the market today or waiting for newer games to be released, give six siege a try, I can guarantee that you won't regret it, the game can be overwhelming at start but once you get the hang of the game it becomes extremely fun.

This is quite a difficult review for me.
I want to recommend but it's just so unbelievebly boring that I can't bring myself to recommend it.
Looking at pre-release content and post-release streams this game really does look sick.
Now that I've actually played is this game really isn't that good at all... :/
And in my opinion, the first was way better.
There is a lot to like here though!
Lots of super cool weapons, lots of different enemies, large levels, and the game runs buttery smooth even on launch day!
A lot has changed since shadow warrior 1 but I feel like some of the changes are questional to say the least.
For starters, the levels are massive and filled to the brim with a wide variety of of enemies.
Because the levels are so big this game often turns into, kite them all around and shoot random explosive barrels that are scattered everywhere.
The co-op just just gives the monsters more HP which in the end doesn't even make it harder, it just takes longer.
And when you get in the situation where everyone went in a different direction and pulls a whole bunch of enemies the game turns into this really bizzare game of, keep running around in circles and shoot whenever you can.
Problem is that these situations can last up to a good 15 minutes...
A big new thing in SW2 is the gemming and resistance system.
Think borderlands, where a sniper rifle that shoots fire-bullets barely does damage to enemies that are on fire, but absolutely decimates ice-type enemies.
That's pretty much what you have here.
It sounds neat in theory because it forces you to take a balanced loadout but it doesn't help make the game more engaging at all.
You're just rotating weapons depending on whatever enemy is following you and the worst part is that most weapons aren't even that good.
A very effective way to play is to take your melee weapon, run away from your enemy while charging a frontal piercing attack, and when it's charged, turn around, do the attack and repeat the process.
It's so effective that even in a 4 man group when enemies get stuck inside a building you're better  off doing this melee charging rather than use bullets.
Which brings up another problem.
The difficulty is a complete joke.
This game isn't hard AT ALL, even on higher difficulties it's not that difficult once you get the hang of kiting mobs around. (ye, like an MMO)
The higher the difficulty the more HP enemies have which just means that you'll be charging more melee attacks.
Now I'm not saying the weapons are bad. some weapons are quite strong even but the down-side is that they♥♥♥♥♥♥ammo like you wouldn't believe.
So, on the highest difficulty you're pretty much ammo starved quite often which is why you keep your trusty ol' melee weapon at hand.
My biggest problem with this enemies so far is the Physical Resistance.
This is some grade-A BS right there...
Enemies with physical resist take next to no damage from bullets and melee attacks and instead take most of their damage from the elemental upgrades you put on your weapons. (which isn't a lot of damage I have to say)
There's this one time my group was fighting in a mine and in the mine were a few massive enemies that charge at you for a lot of damage on top of which all of them had Physical Resistance up the wazoo.
So you have to keep moving and melee is not really an option because you'll get wrecked.
We spend almost half an hour running around in circles shooting these enemies that have just a ridiculous amount of health and in the end they didn't even drop anything good.
And that brings me to the biggest problem with this game.
The loot...
Enemies randomly drop gems that you can stuff in your weapons to make them do more damage, reload faster, shoot fire-bullets, dual wield, etc etc.
The higher the game's difficulty, the better the loot.
But the gems only increases your damage by a little bit but it doesn't change the fact that enemies are still massive bullet spunges.
And there are WAY too many gems in this game.
I don't even know what half of this crap is used for because some of these gems are so bad there is no real use for them.
So before you go out on missions you're forced to sift through the trash to find the gems that are useful so you do decent damage.
New weapons are obtained by doing side-missions which are literal fetch-quests, others can be found and some can be bought in the shop with in-game cash (there are NO microtransactions so let that be noted :p)
There are some really cool guns in this game, there's no denying that :D
It's just such a damn shame you can't use the majority of your weapons whenever you want because maybe your favourite weapon has a bad elemental damage upgrade on it.
I look at my list of weapons and think to myself, ok, this weapon does fire, this one ice, that one toxic, this is electric, that one explodes and is for AoE... I could take that weapon because it looks sick, but damn the DPS is kinda low so I'd better not.
======================================================
I know I'm really ragging on this game and I don't mean to.
You look at the screenshots, you look at the videos and you see a dude using a shotgun to blast a massive hole in a medusa looking thing.
Look sick right? :D
Or grab your wolverine claws and go to town, chopping dudes up left right and center.
That's awesome!!
But in reality, you're not looking at the holes you made in your enemies, you're not looking at the limbs flying everywhere or the massive explosions going off all over the place.
Your looking at the health bar and the damage numbers to figure out which weapon you have on you is best suited to kill this enemy.
And that is why I can't give this game a positive review.
This game could be really fun. chopping up dudes with your friends? that's awesome.
But in reality we're all running in circles asking who brought a weapon that does electric damage while the rest is doing 20 damage per shot on enemies that might actually have a hundred thousand HP...
The elemental system ruined this game for me personally.
If that system would be gone I would have no problem recommending this game.

Since it shares a lot with DOOM (both in style + in my eyes two of the best shooters of 2016) I'm going to do a comparison list.
There is lot of reviews for SW2, but maybe this will offer a different angle for people who have played Doom & on fence about this game. Or on fence about which game to get.
- Very well optimized
- Good graphics
- Relatively bug-free
- Very good selection of PC style graphics & HUD options
- Gore, and some more gore
- Old school, balls-to-the-wall action, little to none BS exposition
- Fast and fluid movement
- Various difficulty levels, that range from easy to very challenging
- No manual saving, checkpoint system
- Both have open levels, that encourage exploration & have secrets
- The movement is even more fluid, even less limits than Doom
- Melee combat. While Glory Kills in Doom are good, SW2 takes melee to another level.
- More detailed gore. It's not scripted like in Doom, you can blast a hole into a big monster, and shoot through that hole at another enemy. Or cut off a leg, so enemy can't walk
- Amount of weapons. SW2 has 70+ different weapons, that all have custom look and animations
- The full campaign can be played with up to 4 player Coop (difficulty scales for it)
- Every cutscene can be skipped. Doom locks you in a room few times & forces exposition
- Enemies are actually "scarier" and more repulsive. You want to really kill those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s.
- More enemy types, while Doom has enough.
- Humour if you happen to like the style of it. Prepare for barrage of dickjokes
- Cheap price. It could easily be full priced like Doom, for some odd reason it's not
- Better replay value. Monster placement is random, while in Doom some enemies spawn in 100% scripted location. Doom has replay value too though, it's largely not scripted either
- Starting pistol is .44 Magnum. Doom's only unimpressive gun is the starting peashooter
- Gun sounds. They lack some low end punch, while they are ok
- Music. The 80's metal menu music is sadly best song of SW2. Mostly it's pretty generic background thing. Doom has better music, while there is some style similarities
- Not sure if can be considered as downside, but there is even TOO much different unlocks and loot. At some point you don't know anymore what to do with them & kinda stop caring
- Character models in cutscenes aren't maybe AAA quality as rest of the graphics
- SW2 isn't serious. It's filled with politically incorrect humour, F-word usage and dickjokes. I found it hilarious, some might not
- Levels are more colorful and varied. Doom less so, with basically 2 looks (Mars and Hell)
- More emphasis on looting and customizing weapons, more like mix of Borderlands and Doom
- No PvP Multiplayer. Won't count it as a flaw, because Doom MP is nothing to write home about. Doom is mainly acclaimed for it's SP campaign
If you can't decide between Doom or this, hope this helped. If you can, get both.

I have completed the Shovel Knight campaign and the Spetre Knight one, and I can honestly say that this is one of the best games I have ever played! I have been submerged in the game for a number of days now. I have barely scratched the surface and yet I have about 50 hours on each of two worlds I have created. The 3D aspect is a lot of fun, and the world shaping and stuff just eats up my time. I level hills, fill in valleys, build walls, make neat tunnels, etc. I have never played Minecraft, but my understanding is that the movement and shaping in FCE is much faster and easier. I guess it looks similar but does play very different from my understanding.
All in all I have really been enjoying the challenge of finding the ore, building up enough to work to automating getting it to the surface so I can smelt it and then use it for research and more building stuff.
I would recommend watching a play through or two on youtube, there are some great folks there. Even though the game has changed over time the mechanics are mainly unchanged so you get a good feel for how much there is to do and to play with!

I give this game a 3 out or 5.
First off, I was buying it as something to play for/with my 2.5-year-old when we're stuck inside and she starts fussing about wanting to "play computer".  There aren't many games on Steam designed for little kids, so I ended up getting this one (on sale, naturally).
The good news is, my daughter loved it.  She calls it the "teddy game" now.
The bad news is, it's not at all what I'd expected.  I'd been hoping for a game that was sort of free-form, where if you clicked on a bird or something in the background, it tweeted and hopped or something.  There's none of that.  The background art is bright-colored and lovely, but it's completely non-interactive.  The game itself is incredibly linear, to the point where if you don't talk to the right person in the right order, you can't go on to another screen -- even if you've already effectively been told you need to go there.
The minigames were too old for my daughter now (not a negative -- I'd expected that) but would probably work for a 4-5 year-old.  Be aware: the voice acting is ATROCIOUS.  That didn't bother my daughter, but my husband and I had to work to keep from laughing.  Also, keep in mind that the game is quite short.
Given the total lack of games on Steam designed for little kids, I'd modestly recommend this game -- but buy it at a discount, not for full price.

I don't know what other reviewers were expecting from DNF, but all I wanted was a Duke Nukem game, and I got exactly what I was waiting fourteen years for.  It's not groundbreaking, and the game shows its long development cycle, but the elements that made DN3D groundbreaking are all there.  The humor, the heavily interactive environment (which few games even now bother to have learned from DN3D), the references (something I dearly love), the crazy enemies, the zany weapons, Duke and friends' over-the-top personalities; everything you could ask of Duke Nukem.  The love and care of the developers is obviously present, even if the game shows its age.
Now, if you get terribly upset about the objectification of women or swearing, just walk away now.  There's nothing in Duke Nukem for you.  But for those of us who've kept the faith, who cut our teeth on Roddy Piper and Bruce Campbell, the Duke is back in fine form.
It's not perfect, not even after fourteen years.  But I really like it.

Below is a list of issues that I have found (no particular order):
- Some keys don't work correctly
- Indicators can be buggy
- AI are useless

- Camera is extremely dodgy and you can't seem to auto centre it

- If in full screen mode the mouse curser and registration box are off (have to have your curser to the left of what you are trying to click).
- If you put the game in window mode (fixes the issue above) and resize it as soon as you load or open a menu it resizes the window back to the small box before you resized it.

- When creating a profile if you select your start/home location first it skips you being able to edit the profiles name (have to go back to main menu to edit it). This is just a bit of a pain.
- Can’t move the seat or steering wheel (Feels uncomfortable)
- Only two buses
This game has got some good points which you can find below however they don’t make up for the issues it has.
- Good looks on weather systems

If you are one of the many who played the original Two Worlds for as long as you could tolerate it before deciding it was a horrific waste of good code,
let that experience keep you away from Two Worlds 2.
I have been playing RPG's (pnp and pc/console) for a quarter century now and I have to say that I love just about every type of pc rpg, from diablo clones to the Wizardy series, and the Elder Scrolls to Neverwinter Nights.  Like many rpg fans, I played the original Two Worlds, and like many, the game cd for the 360 became a drink coaster, and I have to admit that it is a much better coaster than it was a game.
Two Worlds 2 is not that.  While it will only show that I have an hour or two played, I previously owned the game for the 360, and liked it enough that I picked it up on sale here on Steam.  If you set your expectations properly, Two Worlds 2 is a great purchase.  Realize that you are not buying Skyrim.  This is not one of the top ten pc RPG's of all time.  At the same time, it is not Two Worlds either.
Two Worlds 2 is an enjoyable RPG experience, with a fair bit of replay value.  There are far worse ways to spend your money at Steam, and at a sale price, this game is a steal looking at it from a hours played/dollars spent ratio.

know it was a half-hearted port from a mobile game developed for touch screens. While it plays better than almost any other strategy game out there
, the original format really limits the gameplay and UI, relative to true PC titles.
+ Difficulty settings never affect damage, morale, etc. The game is always fair, the only change is the AI.
+ The AI is extremely well made, and extremely tough to beat. It's almost like facing another player.
+ The game relies much more on proper tactics (flanking, pinning down, etc.) than "rock paper scissor" 'tactics' (attack X with Y to win).
+ The graphics are simple and clean.
+ The audio, overall immersion, and historical accuracy is great.
- The UI/HUD is extremely limited due to the touch-screen style.
- Basic info on the battlefield is lacking. You can't see where and how your troops will deploy at their destination, or a list of your units, or a minimap, for instance.
- Your troops tend to act on their own in every situation you don't want them to, and sit idly by when you do. They'll abort a charge half way through, and turn towards an enemy when you want them in an orderly line, yet they often won't return fire. Coupled with the poor UI and no minimap, you often find your units halted halfway across the map when you expected them to act as reinforcements.
- The simplistic graphics are too simple, and units can walk straight over houses.
Save your money and buy this game for its intended mobile platform instead. Unless you own an Apple product that is. Apple went full on SJW and banned all games with the CSA in them. So if that's the case, I guess buy it on steam.

The bottom line:  Missing content and instability aside, the long-term outlook for this game is really mixed.  The skill point system prevents even low aims from being accomplished, not logging in promptly at the same time every day is a gamebreaker for anyone even dabbling in farming, and the systems that the developers want to build into the game effectively ruin the base (very entertaining) game.
So, I played this game a lot in a very short period of time.  I tried to be a yeoman farmer, living independently near a settlement.  My aims were small:  build hut, farm, and eventually dabble in some tailoring and cooking.  However, doing this with less than an entire village proved nearly impossible, as the skill cap does not allow for persuing more than one or two skill lines!  This is despite my perfered server having a slightly higher skill cap than baseline, and signifigantly faster skill development, and entire skill lines not added into the game yet.  Should the developers keep their limited skill cap and extremely slow skill development, this game will become grind-tastic in the worst way.  A farmer could do nothing but farm.  A smith could do nothing but smith.  Neither could fight, or make their own houses and equipment, or do anything but their perscribed role.  In short, it would be boring.
Further, the game just doesn't tell you things.  For instance, how farm crops rot on in the fields after maybe an hour of being harvestable.  So, in addition to farmers being completely ruined by IRL rush-hour traffic, beginners have NO chance of finding out about this until hours of work is ruined.  I can only imagine that feeding your animals, including your precious warhorse, will be similarly time-sensitive.  Frankly, any online game where you cannot miss a single day is not a game I want to play.
These things may change.  This game is an alpha, and the whole system could be patched to perfection tomorrow, for all I know.  However, these problems are not alpha related.   These are features the developers want to put in the final game which could easily ruin it for players like myself.  Further, if the rumors that the developers don't take criticism well prove true, these problems may get compounded by others over time.  For a game that is so broad, open, and free to then turn around and limit player's options both in and out of game is both worrisome and, frankly, stupid.

A great story, with good characters, almost ruined by a game.
I want to love this game.  The story is engaging, I keep saying 'I want to know what happens next.'  You are a horseman of the apocalypse, which for some reason in the universe of this game are the guardians of the balance between heaven and hell.  Well someone messed that up, destroyed all mankind, and framed the rider War for screwing everything.  You are War, find the party responsible, make them pay.  Lots of twists and turns on that path, you'll honestly like a few demons, give others the finger, and laugh with glee while gunning down angels.
The visuals are impressive, remember all the World of Warcraft art with all the highly detailed armor?  Remember how that game looks nothing like that art?  This one does.  This looks like that.  This is the game that wanted to be visually.  Very pretty to look at, glorious in motion especially on PC without any framerate loss.
There are two problems.  First, they decided they wanted to make a puzzle platformer.  Wonderful bits of swordplay are interrupted by seriously overly long puzzle sections of tedius boredom.  Hope you like backtracking!  Seriously, you are forced to backtrack an absurd amount, and sometimes the path to where you need to be gets very confusing.  Prepare for lots of frustration before you get to the next stabby bit.
Second, they decided they wanted to add tons and tons of stuff.  We're talking hey!  Giant sword!  Cool, now give him a killer boomerang thing!  Awesome, but how about a gun?  Can we give him a gun?  Awesome!  But you know every good hero has a grappling gun, give him one of those!  Coded!  Great!  Now hey... There's this game called portal, maybe we should play with portals too?  BAM!  Portal gun added!  Sooo....  Let's drop the bass, give this guy a literal warhorn too!  A little odd but, done!  Now quests for collectables that require backtracking to every single game section after you acquire all this stuff!  Not to say how annoying it is to try to use it all in combat.
The controls are a little iffy, the camera likes to do perspective changes while you are trying to do percise platform jumping, which is a bit maddening.  Thankfully the game is very forgiving of the inevitable falls into endless pits, a small health penalty and puts you right back where you were this time knowing what the camera is about to do to you mid jump.  For the non platform sections?  Controls work fine.  With two exceptions.
1.  The game really needs a 360 controller.  The complicated mess of all the STUFF they want you to do is incredibly awkward on a keyboard.
2.  The range weapon controls are beyond terrible.  Going into aim mode makes you turn slower than molasses, and you need to hit things moving at full speed.  Makes you very thankful to get back to bashing things with your giant sword.
Then there is the purchase new combos option, which most tend to fall into two categories.  Too time consuming and or difficult to trigger mid combat, or way too easy to tigger mid combat so you're always going moves that take you in a direction you didn't want to go.  Thankfully the devs made the game smart enough not to let you fly off a cliff because you were doing a combo.  So go for the ledge fights, just keep well clear of the jump button.
One more note is stability.  The windows port is known for crashing.  But there is no pattern to this, all gamers report crashes at different spots with really no perdictibility.  In my experience I've had something like 6 game crashes in 13  hours.  I would say 3 were alt-tab related.  I also had a 4 hour flawless session that spawned multiple levels.  So be prepared, you will lose progress time to time.
The recommend yes/no system is a bit too limiting, I'd put this game at 75%.  Not enough to tell everyone to go get it, but if you want lots of puzzles with your hack and slash then pick it up.
