It's like minecraft, but without all the boring♥♥♥♥♥♥
Dear lord, this game is fun. It has all of the creative potential of minecraft, but automation removes all the boring negatives like manually mining and smelting and even building block by block. Instead of wasting time on that boring nonsense, FortressCraft Evolved allows you to focus on advancing your tech, building your base, and defeating your enemies!
There are tons of awesome aspects of the tech aspect of this game, with my favorite being the ability to build blocks from a specified block to your location using control-click. AFAIK, minecraft doesn't let you do this. At least, it didn't back in the day when I played it. Also, this game has a grappling hook. Let me repeat that for you. THIS GAME HAS A GRAPPLING HOOK. AND YOU DON'T EVEN HAVE TO UNLOCK IT. There are multiple power source types for your machine, and your enemies (bees native to the world you're stranded on) provide you with valuable building materials. There's a lot of variety in every aspect of the game: building, smelting, mining, etc.
Also, this game is gorgeous for what it is. I'm running it on an intel g3258 that I haven't gotten around to overclocking yet and an AMD r9 270 and it still runs decently on high-ish settings. And it works on linux! :D
There are a lot of complaints from earlier in the game's development about the creator abandoning the project. He came back, and has been consistently releasing updates since the beginning of the year. He's a bit snarky, but he's really fun to interact with, and he actually listens to player feedback.
Basically, this game is everything an indy game should be. Fun, inventive, varied, cheap, and available across all platforms. What are you waiting for?? Buy it!

How far have we come in this legendary game series? Shadow Warrior was originally one of the first FPS games to come out along with Doom and Wolfenstien. Today we now have 3D graphics, amazing gameplay, and more wang then you can handle. This is Shadow Warrior 2! It has all you love about the originals, except with a Diablo style loot system. Most of the loot is upgrades which you can put on your weapon throughout your journey. The weapon system is a bit more stretched as you can now pick up weapons from more powerful enemies throughout the game, like bosses or named enemies. The gameplay remains mostly unchanged from Shadow Warrior 1 but now it plays like an RPG, which works suprisingly well for this kind of game. Money can now be used to buy weapons and upgrades. The weapons are anything short of satisfying. Your weapons come down to swords, pistols, smgs/assualt rifles, shotguns, heavy weapons, and chainsaws/gauntlets. Chainsaws work a lot like swords but they can now be dragged on for more damage. The game's highlights are pretty strong, fast paced action hack n slash mixed with shooting that will leave you running for the next fight. The story is there but it's not a main highlight except for Lo Wang and his new companion's conversations which is pretty funny. Fortune cookies are scattered around the map for some good laughs. Should you buy this game? Yes

Fantastic game that  is an improvement to the first game in almost every way, Also Stan Bush literally recorded a new song for this game that alone should sell you on it.
I was a bit worried when i heard shadow warrior 2 was going to be a looter shooter as i am not that big a fan of games like borderlands however i decided to give the game a try. My fears were quickly put to rest when i was reminded just how fun it is to cut up demons with a big sword, the swordplay feels better and more precise than ever and i no longer feel i have to move the camera all the way up to do a vertical slash. The gunplay is also an improvement over the first with a very large assortment of different weapons and while some weapons feel very similar to eachother the majority feel very unique.
While the first game followed very linear level design the levels in this game are a lot more open and a lot more vertical, due to the huge increase in level size from the first game Wang has been given a double jump and a vastly improved dash allowing you to move extremely quick. The verticality of this game really sets apart the levels from its predecessor it feels great going from rooftop to rooftop during fights and being able to escape to the ground or onto a roof is awesome.
A few of the levels especially the city ones can feel a bit samey especially towards the end of the game but the masssive ammount of enemy variety helps make some of the samey levels feel a little bit different and while some of the levels feel this way there are plenty that feel very unique, early on there was a level that mostly consisted of a massive dojo where almost every wall can be dashed through and destroyed which feels pretty badass.
The looting aspect of the game is a bit weak compared to the rest of the game but still servicable. Loot is really thrown at you in huge ammounts especially when you start fighting elite enemies and bosses you can expect bosses to go full diablo and just explode into loot it feels too common. Towards the end of the game i was getting 50-100 pieces of loot per mission so i find it best to only check what would be an upgrade at the end of a mission or every few missions otherwise you will be in the menu all the time and that aint a place you want to be. I think the menu needs a bit of work sorting loot by item level is a pain selling loot is a pain and there is no way to compare upgrades on a weapon without taking the upgrade out. The loot itself is only upgrades that you can socket into your guns or swords the vast majority of this is just flat number increases such as damage or higher clip size but there are a few interesting ones such as dual weilding or throwing your rocket launcher on the floor to act as an auto turret.
The story like the first is utter utter cheese but lets be honest those are the best kinds of stories, without giving too much away it's set 5 years after the end of the first game and goes even further off the rails. The dynamic of pure hatred the 2 main characters have for eachother results in a lot of  very funny back and forth banter alongside the huge ammount of one liners and Wang jokes from Wang.
The game runs flawlessly for me on a 980ti and a 5930k if i uncap the framerate i get  over 100 fps in every area on 1080p ultra and capped at 60 it didnt go below once considering how great the game looks and how much more open and vertical the levels are compared to the first game the performance is very impressive.
All in all i absolutely loved this game, in a time where the majority of games have a very serious tone it's great that we can still have games that are just pure dumb fun now buy this dumb game for an authentic ninja experience, personally i'd buy it for the new Stan Bush song alone.

Shovel Knight is a blast.  Seriously, that's probably the best way to put it.  It's the sort of game where you look up after a level and it's 2 in the morning because it's so fun and addictive.  Gameplay wise, it's a relatively simple action platformer where you have two buttons besides WASD, jump and attack.  It's really simple and really intuitive.  As the game goes on, you get upgrades for better mobility or better attacks, although most of these upgrades are just ok, and you'll just use like 3 of them regularly.  However, the game is rather unforgiving.  Fair, but unforgiving.  When you die, it feels like your fault, not the games, which imo makes all the difference.  You then lose some gold and respawn at a checkpoint and if you make it to the place where you died, you can get your gold back, Dark Souls Style.  I died around 200 times each for the first two campaigns (more on that later), but in the third, newest campaign, I only died about 80 times, a combination of the third campaign being imo easier and shorter, but partially because I got better at the game.  The boss battles and stages are all unique and well designed, although some bosses feel really hard compared to others, but thankfully those bosses come near the end.
Something that really stands out in the whole game is the level design.  The levels are designed to teach the player without the use of tutorials or hand holding.  The player organically figures out the controls and the moves by themselves.
There are (currently) three campaigns, Shovel of hope, plague of shadows, and specter of torment.  All three are good and worth your while, and each have different stories and different main charaters with different abilities.
Shovel of Hope:  You have to beat this one to unlock the other two, and it's solid.  You play the titular shovel knight as he goes on a quest to defeat the evil enchantress and her Order of No Quarter.  Shovel Knight is probably the worst at combat, but he's no slacker, especially once you get some relics and upgrades.  He is the best at controlling the character when platforming.  He moves intuitively, and is really simple to understand.  Really awesome to play through.
Plague of Shadows: This follows the same levels and map as Shovel of Hope, but this time, you play as Plague Knight, one of the bosses from the first campaign.  He's kinda similar, but very different.  He's better at some combat, but at other times, he's worse.  The same goes for his platforming, sometimes you can sail over obstacles, other times you're frustrated with the simplest things that shovel knight could do easily.  Overall, he's harder to control, but has a lot more options, especially in the combat mode, b/c he can change his basic attack to many different types, only some of which are useful.  Overall, really great.
Specter of Torment:  I'm conflicted by this.  On one hand it's the shortest and easiest campaign, but on the other, I had a blast playing it.  You play specter knight, another boss from the other campaigns, and the story is a prequel to the original campaign.  The levels are set in the same environments, but totally different, with new mechanics and enemies.  Even the bosses get a retrofit.  However, Specter knight is great at combat and great at platforming in certain areas where you're supposed to be.  Without certain helps, he's by far the least mobile knight.  I didn't really have much trouble with the bosses, only the penultimate boss gave me any trouble, and the final boss was almost laughablely easy.  The story is better though, giving more depth to many of the main characters.  It's still awesome, and I really love this campaign.
Also, after every campaign, you unlock challenges (Which are flipping hard, btw.  Except for specter knight's.  Again, idk if I just got better, or if he's just op) and a new game plus, which makes it harder.  Also, a fourth campaign and a battle mode is upcoming for free so long as you own it.  So overall, BUY THIS GAME.  Seriously, this game gives you so much bang for your buck, and it's a blast to play.  9/10

I've been playing this game since it's release. This is a pure masterpiece. Not only it is classic NES nostalgia for many (not for me though, I started with the SNES) but it is a great game overall.
Platform game at its best with great characters, good story, amazing soundtrack that you'll be humming everytime.
One complaint I heard is about the difficulty and it worried a bit too me too since a lot of this indie game going for the nostalgia factor are sometimes too hard, most of the time unfairly.
However this is the erfect example of challenging rather than hard, in which the frustration kicks in very late and it is more about doing the right jump, avoiding the hit at the right time and learning the best strategy to kill the boss.
Also one amazing fact: the developers release every DLC for free and they are actually full new campaigns! At the moment there are two: Plague of Shadows and Specter of Torment.
The first is mostly a re-skin version of the original campaing with a new playable character, Plague Knight, and new mechanics. It is however a new story, very funny also and well done, possibly set at the same time the events of the main game happens, more or less. It has a lot of great moments and it features also new boss battles.
Specter of Torment is a prequel and this feels more like a completely new game. You play as Specter Knight and you still have to defeat all the bosses. However this time the levels layouts are completely different and their respective bosses have new strategies. It is more fast paced than the previous two. This time the humour is more dark than usual and the story it is also a bit more tragic. Even if it is amazing as a DLC, I have really few minor issues: the first is that the soundtrack changed. The tracks are basically the same but with different notes and pitchs compared to the original. Even if it is still good, some of them are not as great as the original.
The second issue is that it seems a bit easier. At the moment, I barely died more than twice per level and the boss feels weak. This might be also for how cheap it is to buy new power up. The costumes can be easily unlocked just before halfway through, even less if you are going to revisit a level for the collectibles.
However, as I say this is a very minor issues compared to how great this videogame is! I can wait for the King Knight DLC!
PS- The Treasur Trove's release also offer Co-op but unfortunately I haven't try it yet.

Review code was supplied by developer/publisher free of charge.
Video:
Plot/Overview:  Just drive.  You're the getaway driver for a string of robberies.  This is an arcade driving game still in early access.  The driving is mixed with twin stick shooting elements.  Earn money to upgrade and buy new rides.
Menus:  The menus are laid out pretty nicely.  Settings has your standard options, sliders for sfx and music.  The video options are lacking however, only three quality levels, an option for full-screen, resolutions that go up to 4k, and an FPS lock, which is locked to 30 or 60 frames.  The garage screen lets you customize your rides and upgrade their turbo, armor, and firepower, as well as equip perks.  The car shop is self explainatory, you buy new cars here.  The statistics show your stats on each map.  There is no ability to rebind keys at this time.
Music/Sound: The music provided by DKSTR is amazing and fits the game great.  My problem with the music, is there isn't a lot of it in the game yet, and it tends to be overly loud even with the settings turned down.  The sound effects are also really well done and fit the game.  Get used to hearing sirens and gunfire.
Gameplay:  This is where the game shines, each vehicle controls differently, the heavy cars like the van and truck are clunky on purpose and are heavily armored, while the more lighter weight sports cars can't take too many hits but move and control crisply.  The shooting mechanic is well implemented but can be tricky when you're trying to dodge traffic and officers.  At the time of this review, there are only two maps available, Test Drive and Martins Valley.  I strongly suggest playing with a controller.
Controls:  I highly suggest playing with a controller.  While playing with a keyboard and mouse is perfectly functional, you get more precision with a controller.  Also, no ability to rebind any of the keys.
TLDR
Pros:
Great controls
Great music and sound
Solid gameplay
Nearly weekly updates
Simple, but effective art style
Cons:
Limited content at time of review.
Music tends to be overly loud.

When it comes to letting their emotions run away with them, humans are their own worst enemy. If they believe something long enough, they will eventually find a way to make it come true. For that reason, there are people who REFUSE to play this game because of the hype on how scary it is…but…is it really?
The premise of Amnesia is simple. You play as a character named Daniel who wakes up in a castle and doesn’t remember who he is or how he got there. Throughout the game you’ll discover clues as to what is really going on. It’s a first person adventure, note that I didn’t say shooter. That’s right…no guns.

In fact, all you are armed with is a lantern that consumes oil which you will need to replenish if you plan on using it regularly. You also get matchboxes that have a one time use in lighting a candle or fireplace within the environment. As you may have deduced by the pictures you glanced at before you started reading this article (admit it, you did), Amnesia is a dark, dark game. You will not have enough oil to keep your lantern equipped constantly or find enough matchboxes to light every single candle or fireplace you come across. Needless to say, it’s wise to use your items sparingly.
For those of you afraid to get the game because of the fear factor, my advice is to suck it up and play it. The fear is more derived from your own mind than it is from the game itself. At first, I was hiding for almost five minutes straight at the slightest movement or sound. It made for an excellent experience however I wasn’t getting anywhere in the game. You have to go into the game with the thought of it being just a game somewhere in the forefront of your mind. “If you die, so what? It’s just a game.” Unfortunately, this takes away from the very experience the game tries to draw you into. If you can find a balance between remembering that this is a game but still be into it enough to crap your pants every now and again, you’ll find the progression to be enjoyable.

This is a review of an early access title, all work shown is subject to change and the review is on the 0.1.8.0 version.
I have spent a few hours on this game and here is what i thought;
After jumping into this open forest i had absolutley no clue what i was doing. The help guide seems to be lacking some things to tell you, such as what to actually do. I spent a good twenty minutes running around wondering what to do, lucky enough i met a friendly player and he sent me on my way with the knowledge of how to collect and craft. I then started my adventure in this very big (and very green) world before i got bored and realised that this game is NOT meant for singplayer, you NEED people to play it with. So after getting some people from my ESO guild we went on our way scouting for a good location which is when we stumbled upon a moose, a wolf and lake which at first seemed like the start of a bad joke but I soon realised that wolves were no joke in this game. After a insanley glitchy fight, some crazy server lag and a respawn we eventually met up and continued our journey for our future home, where we came upon a nice ridge on the mountain and prepared for the vibrant town to come alive before us! ....four hours later we had a nice mine and bit of flat land set up. This game requires patience, a lot of it. This game isn't meant to be an easy rush to be the best, it is hard and I'm glad as nothing is more rewarding then seeing a town come to life that you started from the bottom up! To get more into our review of the game we decided to cut a corner and move into our friends village which was situationed on the Island off the coast of the main land, we arrived to see a nice little set up and decided that five of us wouldn't be able to do it. After some discussions in Global chat we managed to get some lone wolves to come to the town and become a villager, so now I will start my day off tomorrow in my little community.  Me and the fellow villagers then started to discuss the games potential, one point that came up was people claiming lands and creating a kingdom of sorts and a player who has built it all up being the king. This itself would be a very good for the game but then we also thought, with the seige warfare being implemented what if multiple players claimed themself to be the King/Queen, the wars between kingdoms and the borders would be so great so now i would say we are incredibally exicted for what is too come.
So from this gameplay i came to think, as an Early Access  game, this is great. It's got a lot already implemented in the game and has a lot of support behind it to show it hopefully will not become another Stomping Land! But as a game, not so good. So obviously if i was you i would wait, while it has a lot in it at the moment it could use so much more and right now it is just a grind, Always be weary when purchasing Early access!

Pros
-easy controls
-is not wildly inaccurate.  There is no Lee or Meade as they rely on Corps commanders to be on the field.
-strong ai system.  It adapts and will constantly outsmart you on harder difficulties
-can be played through several times. I have finished the battle on day 1 with less tha  10,000 casualties or on day 4 with over 73,000. There are so many different outcomes
-The bonuses for each side are evenly balance (though the US better trained infantry does not make as much sense considering they have been fighting since 1861) thus making it possible for either side to win.
Cons
-still hard to figure out where artillery needs to be placed.  I spend quite some time just shifting artillery around so they can shell the enemy.
-No Full battle or day scenarios.  You cant fight the entire battle of Gettysburg in one go.  The way they have it set up you must fight segments of each day.  Though this can also be seen as a pro as it wouldn't be as hard on the pcs as it would if you had all 160,000 men on the field.
-No chance to capture enemy.  In Sid Meier's you could surround an enemy unit and he would surrender giving you extra points and eliminating them from the rest of the game.  They did not put that in this game so it does get frustrating when you incircle Reynolds corps and watch them rout to safety.

Two Worlds II is only 5 bucks right now, and it's ♥♥♥♥ing worth it. I'm letting you all know, 3 days before the end of the sale.
The story is decent, the voice acting works, it gets a bad rep for being a little different. Also, the AI is hilarious. Sometimes enemies brutally murder you, other times they are completely helpless. It's random and fun.
The graphics are fantastic, the combat system is unique, often difficult to master, but very rewarding. There are no "classes". You just level up and choose where to put your points. You can spec in one type of combat, and you should, but that being said, mages can assasinate using stealth attacks and warriors can summon demons to fight with them. Rangers can snipe and shoot multiple arrows at the same time (and actually aim them at different targets), and the lockpicking system rocks. Mages MAKE THEIR OWN ♥♥♥♥ING SPELLS. Oh and the alchemy rivals that of the witcher and TES.
It's open world, multiplayer (in an entirely different RTS game mode which is sweet), the graphics are gorgeous, the combat system shines, the loot system rocks, you can use a demon eye to float around and scout ahead of you.
Did I mention you can be an actual Bard?? As in, you buy an instrument, and then sheet music, and you get to actually play it. Each instrument has a different style, which you play in a guitar hero like fashion. You can play the drums, the harp, the violin, the flute, and the guitar. The drums are the easiest, and the guitar is the hardest. If you play in crowds, you will actually gain money from the people, depending on your score. Being a bard is so awesome I've literally paused my questing and done nothing else but play, just to try and master it since the moment I discovered it.
Seriously, you are going to want to give this B-sider a shot.

Great game, kind of a weird story though. It's about a growing bear who's parents both die in a viscious car wreck, and Teddy Floppy Ear is faced with a growing issue of mortality. So after their funerals, he goes off on a mountain adventure he promised his parents he would take before they died but sadly couldn't. So with that in mind, he decided to do it in their honor, hoping its what they would had wanted to do. The whole game is a real downer, especially when it starts to heavily revolve around Teddy's confrontation with mortalilty, and living an unhappy life that he wishes he could escape. Other than that I really enjoyed the visceral landscapes, deep story, amazing graphical quality, and the rich lore that surrounds the game. Not to spoil anything but the ending is a nice close to the game, and really opens it up for a sequal (that I hope they make soon) of which could further the story of Teddy's ongoing struggles of discovering himself through his passion of outdoor exploration. I hope you can find the time to pick up this game of the year contender, because it's been a real sleeper hit for quite a long time. Overall 9.8/10

The game is fun but has some glaring issues. The gameplay and mechanics work well but can be hard for new players (example: Zofia has a grenade launcher but can revive herself because why, oh wait in the lore she is a strong character). Another issue is the servers. I mostly have no issues, because 51% is mostly, but when I have issues it is horrible and ruins the experiance. I was just playing and I got disconnected and I couldn't rejoin, so it gave me an "abandon sanction", meaning I can't play or rejoin the match I was kicked from for 15 minutes. The game's player base is growing more toxic and when not toxic one team is always talking about eating someone's♥♥♥♥♥ The game, as said earlier has a plethora of fun, awesome, dazling features and I have met good friends from this game but so many things stick out that need to be patched or fixed. The game also suffers a lot from power creep. The new, very expensive operators always have new abilities or guns that are better then the last, for example Ela has a 51 round 1000rpm SMG and a no skill needed ability. The game's forced micro transactions are bad and come with an "in your face", complicated store front. The characters, especially the DLC operators are a hassle and a grind to obtain. The game has fun mechanics and abilities with a dose of suspenseful action that leaves you on the edge of your seat and that is why I find myself coming back. This game is a great example of going back and fixing and saving a game after it had been shafted by the gaming community and comes with a great DLC plan too. So if you don't mind laggy, slow servers, power creep, highly expensive characters, microtransactions, forced in skins and charms, or inconsistent abilities I can highly recommend this game for you, but if you don't I suggest waiting for the game's problems to be ironed out.
Note: Don't buy the Starter Edition it is a complete rip-off and grind-fest meant to make you want to spend more money to pick up the already highly expensive operators and makes it such a annoyance to even progress.

So, where do we begin? Oh, this game is a f***ing masterpiece.
Let's start with Shovel of Hope. You play as Shovel Knight, in an adventure where you jump, swipe, and pogo across a kingdom to stop the Enchantress/Enchanter (depending on if you use body swap). It is by far my second favorite way to play the game. My only problem is that it's difficulty may put off many people.
Now, on to Plaugue of Shadows. In this one, you go through a storyline alongside Shovel Knight's, and you want to become an all powerful alchemist as you progress through the same levels (with minor differences) as Plauge Knight. In my opinion, this is the worst part of this game, thought I never said it was bad at all. You jump around and use different potions to do different effects. The levels are not all that different, causing many treacherous areas for Shovel Knight to become far too easy for Plauge Knight. I should also add that Plauge Knight is so cute when it comes to interactions with a certain character.
Now, on to Spector of Torment. In this storyline, you go before Shovel Knight's adventure to recruit all of the Order of No Quarter. Jump, slash, and climb in this masterpiece, as you play as Spector Knight. This is a great mix of difficulty and gameplay. All the levels have been completely remade just for Spector Knight. All the boss fights are different as well. My personal favorite part of this DLC is the story that is told for Spector Knight. It is an incredibly sad tale.

After having played Pako - Car Chase Simulator, I knew I had to give Pako 2 a try. With a slightly different concept to the game, it feels much like it's original, while still being unique enough to be it's own game. The controls have been changed, from having a non-stop moving car to having a car that you can control yourself. The weapons have also changed, whereas before you had to pick up ammo off the ground and only shoot it in 1 direction, you are given a gunman who will continuously shoot in the direction of your choosing, either with the mouse or right thumbstick, both of which feel good.
The basics of the game has also changed. In Pako, you simply had to survive for as long as possible while avoiding pretty much everything in the environment, as 1 hit meant you were done. In Pako 2, you get more freedom when it comes to your vehicle blowing up, and can take a few hits before you lose. The premise is also different, as now you must help robbers escape while having cops run after you. I really enjoyed that they added a reason for running away, instead of simply "survive", it's become more of a "help these people out WHILE you survive". It adds a bit of random-ism as well. In Pako, you could simply keep doing a loop around the map until you lost, skipping entire sections of map even. In Pako 2, it forces you to explore everywhere and try out new routes in order to escape the cops.
Overall really fun game, even if it is still in Early Access. The devs are super active on Twitter and they're constantly posting new teasers and screenshots as well as answering questions thrown at them. Definitely worth the buy for those that are looking for a cheap fun game to play!

Sniper Elite V2 is nothing like the original Sniper Elite. This game has kept just the name and the general setting. EVERYTHING else is different. You play an OSS agent sent into Berlin to prevent Nazi scientists from falling into Soviet hands, but you soon discover things are not that simple. You can carry three weapons: a sniper rifle, a sub machine gun, and a pistol, plus some mines, grenades, and such. You need to make your way through enemies (both German and Russian) including infatry and snipers, plus tanks, armored cars, trucks, and more, and accomplish your objective, whether it be assassination, sabotage, or rescue. The best part about this game, is of course, "bullet cam" where you follow your bullet leaving your gun all the way to where it impacts the enemy. With SEV2, you get a new "CSI style" bullet cam that shows you exactly what happened to the target of your bullet, including blood spatter, breaking bones, and ruptured organs, as if you're looking at an X-ray. (You can turn that off if you wish). The game also added "collectibles" (Nazi gold, and wine bottles) to encourage some exploration of the level. There's also various battles against AI and/or playing co-op on certain missions. All in all, SEV2 is a fun game, if a bit watered down from the original sandbox vision. Eye candy, on the other hand, is excellent.

You're an awesome sniper and you're job is to be sneaky and snipe your way through German and/or Russian soldiers while getting to your objectives. The sneaky part is harder than it sounds. The sniping rifles are the main characters in this game, the rest of the guns are not quite as powerful but they do the trick, if you aim right. There are a lot of things to take into account to make the perfect shot count.
The use of sound is quite important in this game, you sometimes will see an indicator on your top-right when a large sound can mask your shots. Trying to time this right was pretty fun, since if your shots are heard the enemy might notice your position rather fast. The AI isn't perfect, I found them running into obstacles and getting stuck once in a while, which was pretty funny but takes away a little of the challenge.

If this was an Early Access game, I would be gobsmacked. However as a full release, there are some glaring flaws I noticed in just the first hour.
Foremost, the tutorial for a game this complicated should continue through the first five hours, lightly stepping in whenever the player encounters a new mechanic to explain it. I spent over an hour in this game trying to do one thing, and one thing only. I wanted to automate power transmission from the main generator to the coal mining drill, and subsequently automate coal transmission from the drill to the generator that burns it. In over an hour, I came no closer to figuring this out than I did watching the video at the top of the page.
Secondly, the crafting system interface needs to be scrapped and redone. Impossible to find crafting requirements without more than a minute of searching through menus and lists, meanwhile 60 percent of the screen is taken up by ridiculous "sci-fi" window borders that do LITERALLY NOTHING AT ALL. If you are going to copy minecraft, at least copy the parts that were user friendly.
Thirdly, do you know why blocks take a few seconds to break in minecraft, but appear instantaneously when building? ITS BECAUSE IT WARNS YOU WHEN YOU HAVE ACCIDENTALLY DONE THE WRONG ACTION. I spent more time than I can measure switching from the thing I actually WANTED to build back to BLOCKS OF DIRT just to fill in A HOLE I DIDNT MEAN TO DIG. This is utterly ridiculous.
HOWEVER
The concept has incredible potential. Adding automation and base defense to a minecraft style operation creates both drama and empowerment, and it would be something I REALLY want to enjoy, but these initial issues with the OBSCENE learning curve, clunky interface, and other oversights overshadow a very good idea. Fix these issues and the game will improve.

Two Worlds II is a solid, if a bit generic, single person RPG.  I have seen comparisons to Skyrim/Elder Scrolls games and will say that I think that is somewhat of an unfair bar with which to compare it.  I played the original Two Worlds and found this to retain some of the nice features of the original (making all materials usable, the ability  to tailor weapons to work best against specific foes) while dumping some of the lesser features (the horse combat, which, while a neat idea, never worked well). The ability to tailor the character skills to my style of play was a definite plus to the game, allowing me to make the character I wanted as opposed to following a class type.  The main storyline was decent, but the side quests, while sometimes fun, were rather generic.
I found the exploration in this game to be rather limited.  Although there were several places the hero could go immediately, there wasn't much to discover at each location.  I was also somewhat disappointed to find that the last island, while seemingly huge on the map, was very limited in where the character could go.
I actually found the Pirates of the Flying Fortress expansion to be more enjoyable than the main game.  Although the gameplay was very similar, I felt the plot that was more absorbing for me (perhaps it is my deep-seated longing to be a pirate of old).  The humor was great and the side quests seemed more engrossing than the main game.
All in all, I can recommend this game when purchased at a discount for someone who is looking for something familiar and somewhat generic to waste a bit of time and follow a story.  I would recommend against it for someone looking for a cutting edge game that has something new (or, had something new 3 years ago).

After a relatively short scene-setting intro and a very quick tutorial, FortressCraft Evolved has handed you the basics and expects you to get on with it, which is a refreshing change from too many games with 20 minute pause-button press-pause tutorials that seem to be the trend recently.
That said, the tutorial does give you the basics of how to figure everything else out for yourself with fairly extensive in-game help and tooltips, so with a bit of trial and error along the way, for which the game imposes no penalties on the easy difficulty settings (my personal recommendation until you know what you're doing), you soon get into the swing of it.
Automation is a major part of the game, and your strategy of implementing this will heavily determine the pace of the game. Want it to go faster? Simply increase whatever factor is limiting your progress, be it power, materials, or machine throughput.
Just as you're getting the hang of all this, you'll come across the Threat Analyser and probably end up building one out of curiosity. This will warn you of incoming attacks and keep you informed as to how much attention your base is drawing from the native life forms. Very useful in determining when you really need to change your focus to building defences against said life forms, but again on the easier settings the only penalty for failure is that it temporarily stops your source of comepletely free power.
I've restarted this game several times now, because after developing my base setup a certain way I get further then come up with a better way to do things, which would almost certainly be easier if I did it from the very beginning. The fact that this game can still cause such epiphanies is to me a mark of a very well thought out game indeed.  That said, I could just tear it all apart with no penalty, and rebuild, but I prefer a clean slate.
The game is undergoiong continual development on a daily basis. This does not mean that the game is unfinished, having watched the developer's daily live streams of the work being done I can say that it if the game had stayed in Early Access until he ran out of ideas and had implemented all the current thoughts he has for late-game content, it would still be Early Access ten years from now, and the game already far surpasses many titles that I've seen launched from EA.
It's true that the developer is planning explansion packs as a way to introduce large chunks of extra content to the game, and a lot of people have slammed this decision, despite the fact that he has clearly said that if he can afford to do so, these will be free expansion packs rather than paid.  Given how many games are released in an almost episodic fashion these days, this is by no means unreasonable, especially given the exceptional value for money the FCE represents. How many games can give hundreds of hours of enjoyment for £10?
At this price give it a try, it's a steal and if you enjoy any kind of tower defence, voxel building, crafting, gathering or logistics/assembly line games you should have a blast.
Tl/dr: A great game that keeps getting better.

This game holds a lot of promise, and it looks like it's going to be a lot of fun. It's richly detailed, and the graphics (for a game of this Minecraft-esque premise) are very good. To say it's even in "alpha" stages, however, strikes me as a gross exaggeration--even in spite of the "early access" label. Basically, all you can do is perform the same limited set of functions over and over, and write bug reports--something that used to earn minimum wage, plus all the coffee you could ever want. Before you shell out $40 for this game, bear in mind that "playing" it constitutes what used to be called a "job" at this point in time. It's very, *very* incomplete, riddled with bugs in every function, undersupported by its help functionality, and exceptionally confusing. In my personal opinion, while--again--it shows every sign of becoming a great game in the future, it's not very entertaining at all as-is, and doesn't merit a price tag at the present time: the developers, if they can't pay someone to play it or handle the playtesting themselves, should be farming it out to family and friends for assistance, or trying to crowdsource additional development/playtesting funds, or doing *something* other than saying "Hey, this is worth $39.99 right now."

While I walked away from Amnesia having enjoyed playing it, I was disappointed with how little the game actually scared me. It does a great job of building tension, but it missed the part where it needs to eventually build up to something, and often times I would clear an entire area/level without actually encountering anything and the game at these moments just felt like a sight-seeing tour. Whats worse is when I did encounter the monster I found it was surprisingly easy to avoid. Just jump into the nearest room and hide and the monster doesn't really make any effort to find you other than standing there for 5 seconds, then turning around and not reappearing for another 40 minutes, sometimes I went 2 hours without another encounter.
Don't get me wrong, nothing is worse than a horror game that constantly shoves monsters in your face because then its just becomes tedious. But I would say the monster in Amnesia needed to have a little more determination in his quest to rip my guts out. That's not to say the game never game scared me, there were 2 genuine points that had me anxious and ended with me scrambling to get a through a door only to find it was locked and I had no choice but to turn and face my inevitable doom.
The 'puzzles' are the strongest point of the game, because they often involve you having to search for parts in various rooms to fix a machine so you can activate it and move on to the next stage, and nothing is worse than having to enter a new room/location and trying to find a specific part while also keeping an eye out for any movement. Having to split your focus like this is what helps to create that stress/tension.
One thing I will strongly criticize is the very beginning sequence. Before you actually play the game it starts off with a cutscene showing your character trying to stay awake as he loses conciousness. During this sequence he reaccounts to himself his name, where he's from, and what year it is while showing a trail of blood behind him as he crawls along the ground (as if to say "SEE THIS TRAIL OF BLOOD? YOU'LL NEED TO FOLLOW THIS ONCE THE GAME STARTS"). If you're gonna call a game 'Amnesia' then it would better to commit to that idea completely, and not just hand that information over to the player before they've put in any effort. Because while the character does not rememeber this information after he's passed out, the player does. This creates an immediate disconnect in the immersion factor. No cutscene and just thrusting the player into the game immediately would of been a better option and more consistent with the title.
With all that said though I enjoyed the game. I liked picking up notes and uncovering the mystery of what happened in the castle, I liked the puzzles, and the game does a decent job of building tension even if the monster sometimes forgets to do his job.

Sit down, son. You just stumbled upon the page of the best shooter ever made. Pay some respect.
Before the days of shooters that holds your hand and aim for you, that regenerate your health and show you what to do like a baby, there was this. Unreal Tournament 2004 - the most brutal, adrenalin-fueled shooter since Quake 3 Arena, a game so fast-paced its guaranteed you'll burn your eyes from not blinking for so long. They say we only use 20% of our brains - well, if you play this game on the hardest difficulty, you'll be using 100% i assure you. Holy hell son, this game uses so much of your brain it pretty much even cures autism. This game is filled with so much testosterone you have to shave your beard every forty minutes of gametime.
Gameplay wise, this game is delicious. With an amazing arsenal of creative, varied and badass weapons, its certified there is a gun for everyone and every situation - sniper rifles that shoot lightning bolts, a triple rocket launcher, jesus christ did i mention a shotgun that shoots grenades too? (The Flak Cannon, considered the number 1 best gun of all times by PC Gamer). Also, with the ability of limitless dodging, walljumping and even double-jumping, the potential for amazing acrobatic moves to evade your enemy's attacks are so great not even Dante from Devil May Cry can keep up. Yep: he cries every night because he cant be as badass as you, when you're playing this game. But this is the bare basic - to survive in the Online arenas, you better be backflipping over your enemies and giving them an instagib headshot while upside down. That's how you play this. However, to be good you have to have absolute keyboard coordination and aiming abilities - it aint easy to do those moves while scoring headshots airborne. Its so hardcore, they say ninjas have to play this game to graduate in Ninja School as their last test. I'm not even kidding.
The maps are varied, from skyscrapers reaching space and low-grav to gothic dungeons, futuristic egyptian pyramids to spaceships blasting in hyperspace - there are over 140 maps in this game (thats almost 5 times more than any CoD), ranging from Deathmatch maps to Capture the Flag, Double Domination, Onslaught (Battlefield-esque map node domination), Assault (from the original UT) and even Bombing Run (Its soccer. WITH GUNS). And kid, that's not even taking into account the thousands of maps released by fans - that's right, the modding community is huge for this game. (No DLC crap, no. You get all those maps and access to mod maps for free. Welcome to oldschool shooters)
The soundtrack and graphics certainly do not falter. We get badass tracks like the one in DM-Asbestos, and others have more epic orchestral music (for actual epic scenes: assaulting an alien mothership to save Earth) and the graphics, for their time, were considered to be amazing (Even modern games, like Killing Floor, use this game engine as base). The visual and audio presentation certainly do not lack, but to this day this game isnt known for having pretty trees, its known for being the best shooter of all times and god damn it does it right.
Together with the classic Unreal Tournament and Quake 3 Arena, Unreal Tournament 2004 is known by shooter veterans worldwide to be the best competitive shooter experience that ever existed. Think you're ready for that? Take off the Angry Birds shirt, the Casual of Duty cap and get ready for a terrific head-hunting experience with the game that INVENTED Double-Kills, Headshots and Killing-Sprees (that all games rip-off nowadays).
Final Score: 10/10

It's very mediocre at best.
-Hit detection is shoddy.
Your chance to hit someone is pretty rare unless you are in melee range, and even then it is a crapshoot whether or not your 30 round clip will register a single solitary hit against your enemy.
-Damage you do seems to be completely random.
From what I've seen, the difference in how much damage you do per shot fluctuates randomly, you can fire at an enemy from a certain distance and kill them in a couple shots the first time around with headshots, and the next time you see them you can hit them an upwards of 5-9 times from the same HP to actually kill them as opposed to the 2 needed before, there is no consistency (Tested with standing targets at the same distance with the same health, and the same weapon with similar latency between players)
-Paying to unlock items way beyond your level that can still be used against new players.
Not going to say Pay to Win nescessarily, however it is a definite advantage over anyone using the lowest tier or starter weapons with absolutely no accuracy or damage output Vs. Mid to high tier weaponry (Provided the RNG damage is more likely in their favor)

asymetrical. One side almost always has a clear advantage in terms of manuvering, cover and objective placement.

First, as a someone who enjoys learning about the Civil War, this game quite literally takes you through the Battle at Gettysburg with unit names and strengths closely matching those actually deployed.  When the troops arrive, including times of day, where and the subsequent battle locations also follow the real battle over its three day course.  All set over geographically accurate terrain.
Second, the game allows for you to influence the battle through each engagement by securing objectives, while still adhering to basic advantages and disadvantages each army held, including as mentioned the initial troop strengths and the arrival of reinforcements.  What your actions accomplish the first day carry over into the second, and so on.
Last, the game play is ponderously slow, RTS, which I found fantastic.  The pace gives time to appreciate the battle, look over the progress and make adjustments accordingly, without having to practice improving hand-eye coordination, key memorization, and so on.  There are a lot of little nuances you can learn over time, and several game play options from either the North or South's perspectives, all of which allow you too improve as a General, take on more difficult AI opponents and add replayability.
I highly recommend this game.

I hate giving this game a negative review, because I really like it. But I've a simple rule: Games that are incomplete and not marked early access get the thumbs down.
There are many resources with descriptions like "not implemented yet" or "has no use yet, but will soon." There are big mechanics of the game (losing a base assault for example) which don't do anything. The game is quite playable and enjoyable, but it's not even in beta yet.
Alot of people were complaining about this game, and honestly I think it was because they didn't understand the mechanics. I remember one guy complaining that generators don't work underground so you can't go very deep... i guess he didn't see all the power transmission devices? But then, blocky games with "craft" in the title are clearly targetting the minecraft audience, and I think this game requires a bit more maturity to understand.
The game really is pretty good, although a bit rough around the edges. I think the game could use a rebalance to make resource management less cumbersome. Specifically, late game components (mk III lasers for example) take quite a few resources to build. But hey, it's an automation game so that's perfectly reasonable, you just need to build more mines. The problem is that if you build enough mines to keep those your factory making those at a reasonable pace, the storage of resources becomes a nightmare.
In my situation, I've got two or three machines making late game components, and my storage facility (which is really big btw) is either completely empty, or overflowing to the point where my transit lines jam up. I'm constantly running up and down my mine to turning drills on and off so that my storage won't overflow, becase honestly (and here's the important part) it's easier to turn them on and off then to make a storage facility large enough to support the flow.
I often see the developer on the forums asking things like "what would you like to see?" I'd like to see cheaper storage and transport in the early game (so you can ramp up faster without all the waiting for tin bars), and higher tier transport and storage in the late game. Just something as simple as a "super hopper" that's expensive but holds 1000 resources would go a long way. A faster transport system then the tubes would be nice too (or maybe mk 4 lasers and more powerful matter-movers). Just something along those lines.
Anyway, that's my take on it. I love the factory games, and this is the best 3D one I've found, although it still has a long way to go. To those who like the automation aspects of this game, do make a point of looking at Factorio though, because it is the best IMHO.

The Roman town of Massilia is under assault from barbarians from Gaul. The Warlord Vindex had brought an army of nearly 3000 warriors, while the general Quintus held the town with 3 hastati with mercenary reinforcements on the way. Vindex began his attack on the town; his army moves up with battering rams to tear down the wooden walls and gate. Quintus and his men hold up near the town center, blocking the narrow streets that lead to it. The mercenary reinforcements have only just begun to arrive on the battlefield and continue to match towards the town. The walls and gate fall and the Gauls begin to flood the town, Vindex stays behind and watches from outside. The Gauls countue to pour into the town and a small group brakes off from the main army. The main army moves down the main road to the town center while the smaller group takes a different road. As the main army gets closer to the town center they are greeted with with volleys of pila fire that shred into the barbarians killing many. The Gauls with their massive army charge into the line of hastati and intense combat fallows. The two units of hastati fight bravely against the Gauls but their numbers are staggering and they slowly push the Romans back. At the same time the smaller army is attacking a seconded point on the road that is less defended but the Romans here are able to hold them. Quintus encourages his men to keep fighting before joining the battle himself to the keep the main army from advancing. As the Romans continue to hold the town center the mercenaries finally arrive to help and see Vindex just outside the walls. Before Vindex can even realize what is happening the mercenaries surround and attack him. Vindex and his body guard fight bravely but are all eventually cut down. The mercenaries quickly move into the town and cut off the Gauls from behind. The Gauls now confused and tired begin to panic and try to pull back but can't as the roads have been blocked. The Romans and mercenaries begin to slaughter the barbarians. When the day was out only 47 men were what remained of Vindex's army. Several months after the battle Quintus would join his father with a massive army to conquer all of Gaul. Quintus would go on to conquer the Iberian Peninsula and revive the title "The Great". As for the mercenaries, they disbanded and settled in Massilia. Years latter their descendants  would help form the very backbone of the legion and lead Rome to further glory.

What can I say about LIfe is Feudal? I bought this the first day it came out on steam. I was a little dissapointed at first after a few hours of play and a few server crashes later. I reminded myself it was an alpha and kept playing. The more I played the more I got addicted to this game, the happier I was with my purchase, and the more I saw it's potential.
This isn't a game that you play solo or to build something "real quick". I found that out on day 1. At the end of day 1 I had some skills up and some tools, but nothing much else accomplished except my guy getting hungry. By day 2 I met some Canadians and we formed a small village. After being raided by other players on day 3 we decided to get our defenses up. Fast forward to today and we have a nice village of about 12 people all working in cooperation. We have blacksmiths, hunters, leatherworkers, Alchemist(me), Farmers and builders. We started building stone walls around our city and watch towers to protect it and armed ourselves with chainmail and pitchforkes. The fun in this game lies in cooperating with other people to build something more than just a small town.
There are some bugs and a few of the skills haven't been implemented yet. That doesn't stop it from being fun as hell to play with a group of people. This game does have some great potential and I hope to see the developers keep at it. Think age of empires meets Ultima Online (before trammel). As long as the devs keep at it I'll be more than happy with the $40.00 I spent on it.

I also think that people have exaggerated their builds/graphics settings a bit. I have a fairly updated computer with a 1070 and it still experienced a bit of graphical lag, especially in the city levels.
Finally the upgrade and loot system. This combined with the skill system just feels so shallow. There's absolutely no HUD element for comparing different upgrades on your weapons and its not exactly an easy task to compare it to what you have (maybe I'm just stupid on that one). All of the upgrades feel like mostly the same thing and you get an absolute shit♥♥♥♥ton of them.
You know how in Borderlands when you find a dropped gun you can easily mouse over it to compare it to what you have?
You know how in Borderlands enemies have fairly clear elemental weaknesses, instead of putting them on a messy, hard-to-read-in-battle HUD element?
You know how in Borderlands every character has their own clear speciality and a direction to go in instead of just being able to go with whatever?
I wouldn't necessarily say Shadow Warrior 2 is a bad game, it's just simple and shallow while at the same time drowning the player in pointless upgrades that after a while feel like too much of a pain to sift through to compare to what you have. After an hour I think about how much I'd rather be playing Borderlands, and I'm not even that big of a Borderlands fan. After 2 hours I'm drained and bored with it. Maybe the game picks up later on but after 5 or so hours of play I have to say I'm not entirely impressed. I wouldn't recommend this at the full price tag, maybe wait a bit and catch it when it's on sale.

I actually do reviews for games on Giant Bomb and PC Gamer... and one game I have trouble reviewing is Amnesia Dark Decent. It's not that I'm indecisive it's just, I can't find the proper words to ever describe this game. You couldn't possibly understand what this game means to me. You might like it and the horror genre would say it's a great game but to me it's more. This game single handedly restored my faith in horror games and got me playing them again. After Resident Evil 5/6 and after Silent Hill Homecoming and Downpour I stopped. Stopped playing, stopped reading up on, stopped caring about horror games. Resident Evil I saw coming but Silent Hill too? This mass appeal mindless action bullsh*t needs to stop. Survival horror was the genre that got me into gaming and then I saw the genre just up and leave us fans for more sales from the Call of Duty players. Action is where it's at? As the head developer for Resi 6 said "Survival Horror games are no longer popular, we needed a new direction and new ideas" well guess what... Amnesia proved Survival Horror still has plenty of new ideas to bring to the genre and proved that the genre is not dead.

Amnesia is art.... it's artwork crafted by brilliant minds. Look past all the fun scary chases and the jumpscares, just look at the game. A first person game that doesn't have weapons? Yeah imagine that. You hide and run from monsters, much like people would do in real life. But if you break down the level design, the choice of imagery, the methodically detailed environments. You will see true beauty within. If I may quote some negative reviews here "water monster wasn't all that great of an enemy, he doesn't even have a character design. It's lazy...." yes they had limited resources however this isn't lazy design choices. The fact that you cannot see the water monster is more terrifying than any other creature in the game. It plays off your imagination, the fear of the unknown. Your mind subconsciously filled the blank with your worst fear which gave this monster so much memorability. The water monster is one of the most memorable moments, everyone talks about it and that's the reason.

After such a horrifying experience with the water monster, what happens? You walk into a well light room with a fountain that supplies the calming sound of running water, a hole in the ceiling with light seeping through (one of the first times you see the light of day in this game), beautiful music plays softly in the background and the room has a tint of blue in the air. This is no randomly designed room, no this is a reward. This is saying "Hey you made it through that horrible experience, breathe relax a bit. You deserve it" and that is something I haven't seen before. No stupid achievement unlocked, no legendary loot, no high score and no misspelled CONGRADURATIONS. In a game that plays on your fear and emotions, they reward with such. They made you crap your pants, now they're making you feel relaxed. And that means more than any achievement.

The story is rich and it plays along with the tension in the game. The enemies aren't scary on the level of a jumpscare but rather the fear of being chased. Jumpscares are cheap thrills, true fear is much harder to achieve in a gamer and much more satisfying for the gamer. They accomplish this in many ways. Never knowing what danger lurks beyond the glow of your lamp, the dark abyss continuously hunts you down, the monsters are not just some scary looking monsters for the sake of "boo look at me I'm scary" they're people you tortured and sacrificed for your own safety against the darkness, their disfigured bodies are representations of the guilt you bare in the deepest parts of your conscious despite suffering Amnesia you still feel it, led astray by someone you thought you could trust, no escape or easy way out the only path is down and it's bathed in darkness as you descend slowly into your past with each step you lost sanity, walls are shaking, the crackling sound of your own mind is louder than your beating heart as you're chased by a horrifying disfigured creature you created, the sound of screeching can be heard when they're getting closer letting you know how close you are to death.

Oh... jeez I... I can go on and on about this game. Hell I want too... but if this gets any longer it will be considered a novel. The best thing I can say about this game? Play it... please. I beg you if you're a fan of horror games, if you like being scared, if you like a good story or immersion or hell if you just want to play a damn good game; play this game!

However, I've seen my mistake. You don't give it a 10 based on some score that means nothing to anyone else other than you. You're giving it a 10 based on the experience the game gave you. Amnesia is an awesome horror game that replaces jumpscares with a creepy, immersive atmosphere. The game includes a lot of puzzles which aren't insanely complex but still require a decent amount of intelligence to complete. Personally I think the story is great, lots of information is scattered around the halls of Brennenburg in the form of notes. These notes are often accompanied by the great dialogue that makes an appearance in the game every so often. The voice acting is brilliant but unfortunately it's not featured as much as I would like it to be, simply because there is a small amount of characters. And of course the monsters... the monsters play a huge role in the game. As if the terrifying atmosphere wasn't enough you will also be filled with paranoia knowing that there could be a monster waiting behind every door you open, every corner you peek around. Arguably the best thing about the game is "Custom stories", there are thousands of levels to download online that are made by the community so that you can keep playing even after you have completed the main story! If you want a horror game that will keep you constantly frightened, but also curious to discover what will happen next then you should definitely try out Amnesia.
Overview
Pros
- Absolutely terrifying atmosphere (better than cliché jumpscares, imo)
- Great story
- Awesome voice acting
- Community made levels, often have amazing stories.
Cons
- Puzzles sometimes become tedious
- No combat (This boils down to preference)

An otherwise bland sniper game made somewhat memorable by its innovative features. V2 is great testicle-shooting fun for about 3 hours, but then it quickly gets overwhelming. Bullet ballistics were advanced and the simulation seemed quite a bit more accurate than other shooters. Getting long-distance kills was very satisfying, mainly because of the gory bullet-cam that displays your bullets entering your opponent's body and wreaking havoc on his organs.
I would have loved for the sniping fun to continue, but all the sudden the game overwhelms you with massive numbers of... tanks. Yes, I said tanks. Literally, you're on the ground with no cover, trying to shoot a tiny fuel cap that will blow the thing up. All while it's pumping you with bullets.
The game also incorporates a story, but it's bland and forgettable. Graphics are on-par with a decent game released in 2009, minus the bullet-cam (best bullet-cam ever).
Multiplayer sucks. You all know how much it hurts to get sniped from across the map within a few seconds of spawning. Imagine this, but in a game with poor level design... where the only class is sniper. That, and there's almost never anyone playing.
The price is horrific. Honestly, don't even think about spending $50 on this. If it goes on sale for under $15, you might want to consider it-- but don't expect too much.

"Nancy Drew: the Ghost of Thornton Hall" ranks in my top five favourite Nancy Drew games produced by Herinteractive. This game is by far the spookiest though, from the random shadows that fleet across the screen to other strange happenings. If you're faint-of-heart, you might like another one of the Nancy Drew games better, or at the very least, don't play this one at night! :-P All-in-all though, the graphics, storyline, and characters are really engaging. Herinteractive really strived to make this game one of their best yet. I have few qualms with the game itself--some of the puzzles were a little too challenging for me, but it's definitely a good brain tease at the very least! Many of the Nancy Drew games recently have really focused on visiting a variety of countries to welcome new cultures to the game. While I fully approve of this notion, some of the games come off as a wee bit stereotyped. This particular game, however, is not one of them. This game has a true sense of place because it's not just aiming to put another Herinteractive flag on the map. The location itself doesn't really pertain much to the game (though it is stated), which in my opinion, makes the gameplay so much more realistic. :-)

Arguably the best of the Unreal Tournament games, which seem to follow a popularity trend similar to that of the Godfather... Taken with Unreal Tournament 3, we can see the sad consequences of a gaming industry that increasingly tries to mimic the film industry (is there a real difference anymore?), though the evidence for that claim is a little more implicit between these two titles... The later has fewer maps: Unreal Tournament 2004 has 106 maps

compared to the 47 that shipped with Unreal Tournament 3

One only needs a brain to realise this is less than half. Furthermore, UT3 spreads these maps over 8 game types compared to 10 in UT2004. Why then did UT3 Cost $60 when new, and UT2004 cost $40 despite having only 3 years between release dates? The obvious answer is, it looks better. Many more people are needed to create a new Engine than are needed to create new maps; many more people mean many more salaries to pay whilst maintaining agreeable profits.
Why should the gamer settle for less and pay more? The argument that better graphics make up for the defecit can easily be exploded by taking it to its logical conclusion: Would one pay a very large amount, say $100 or more, for a photorealistic game that lasted only several hours? If the answer to that is yes, it in turn begs the question: Why not buy a film?
Of course, very little can be done about this trend in practice; big developers will continue to develop, with teams of thousands, games that look fantastic and gross multi-million figures. These games will be short and expensive. These games will have neither pretension nor surplus content (except that that must be brought later). This should not manifest as defeatism however, and least of all complacency.
To undermine this trend, at least in part, one can: Support indie developers by purchasing their games, and being more vocal about them, not pre-order games that promise in advance to be lack-lustre, not pay double the retail price for a bas relief tin and a pamphlet; I am talking here of Legendary Editions and so on (What is legendary about a metal case, art book and a making of... DVD?), be dubious of games released in a yearly fashion, or jack it in all together and find a new hobby.
In any case, UT2004 remains a great game in its own right. The volume of content ensures many unique experiences by definition, and the game still has a strong online aspect to be enjoyed. It is fun in the sadistic way that shooting things is, and it sets itself too few pretensions to have any serious flaws. It discarded very little from the original title and updated the graphics to the standard of the time, and it did this without skimping on the things that make a game a game, namely characters, levels and modes, showing yes- it can be done, so yes- I recommend it.

In the current state of the game, you can do some sandbox survivaley things (gather stuff, craft stuff, walk around, build stuff), however although the basics are there, the game lacks content and gets boring very quickly.
What I mean is that:
-The game world is uniform. Water, trees and rock at different elevations. Abandoned player villages with the same basic buildings in each. Random bags of loot of unknown origin laying all around.
-The game world is static. It seems there IS weather and a day/night cycle of some kind, but their effects on the world are undetectable. It feels as if its a summer day 24/7. And no other kinds of events to drive the game of course.
-The game world is too small, safe, scarcely populated and boring to make village building seem like there is a purpose. You can survive just fine without a village, so why build one? To make shinier weapons you dont need?
Basically there is no incentive to do anything other than boredom. Needs more content, needs more dynamic world, needs more environmental pressure to survive. Something to force you to find or create shelter and keep advancing to stay ahead whatever threat there is.
However, Im sure these problems will be addressed when all the basic game mechanisms are in place.
The sandbox survival crafting aspect is deep and clearly aims for realism (if we ignore alchemism...). Raw materials need to be gathered from different sources in different ways, possibly processed in certain ways and then products can be crafted out of them. Its not oversimplified but not confusing either. Craft an axe out of a stick, rock and some plantstuffs to tie them together, all easily collectable by right clicking the right things. Use axe to cut down trees and slash at people for 5 minutes without them dying and losing all their hard work no matter how hard you try.
The game seeks to simulate all aspects (resources and production, building and terraforming, fighting, nature...) in a reasonably realistic and interesting way, avoiding the use of oversimplified models for anything.
The graphics seem like they will look great with some polish (some gaps in terrain, grass isnt rendered very far which shows, buildings could be rendered further away using impostors or similar...)
UI is fine, some lack of 'smoothness' with switching between free mouse and FPS mode. (since this switch needs to happen all the time for working with the menus and clicking on items). It just feels clumsy in a way.
I cannot say I enjoy the game in the current state (since the lack of content and incentive to progress makes it get boring soon), but after theyve worked some more on the resource/crafting/building aspect, made the world more dangerous and overall more 'alive', it will be a great game.
An aspect I like particularly is that it seems more social than some other similar games. Success requires cooperation (building a village yourself is difficult), and PvP/dying have been made not so lethal (you are stunned before you die), unlike in other games where someone is likely die when two persons meet.
I recommend the game not because it would be that fun to play in the current state for prolonged periods (if you play with friends it will probably be fun), but because it clearly has potential to become great and its halfway there already, and the devs seem like they know what theyre going for and seem to have been successful so far.
Price seems decent since the game is going forward at a steady pace so I dont see it as a 'risky investment' in any way.

An hour in and this feels like more shadow warrior in all the right ways.
20hr 70% UPDATE:
Still enjoying core gameplay. Not a lot of plot, but the dialogue is well done, and as the game goes on there is more depth to the characters. Love the variety of guns and switching them up. Played with the both by selecting thematically for roleplay, and for min/max. Picking just the guns you like the style of is totally doable, but may require more twitch skill if you are not min/maxing with the best drops and highest tier weapons you have. Crafting and gems have serious issues though. Had no problem with level design and the procedural element. I actually quite like most of the designs, at least in terms of the general theming. Have not used coop, certainly doesn't need it.
Totalbiscuit's criticism is all valid, but it does not kill the game for me. His claim that it is unsalvagable is certianly not true for myself. The game is visually busy. The game can be spongey. The loot is fiddly. Do yourself a favor and don't spend time fussing with gems in a level. Would have been nice if there was a crafting station and shooting gallery in the wang cave where this was done. (The gore and slicing physics seems to not apply to the dummies in the hub, which seems like a missed opportunity.) TB is straight wrong about a few things, duel wield for assualt rifles is unlockable late game, there are secrets, and weapon drops are semi predictable through the named boss monster system (red skull on minimap). The criticism is somewhat valid still, as none of this is presented to the player clearly, still not sure if I have seen all the mods yet. (Are there alt fire mode gems?) Gem crafting has no clear guidelines not sure if it is totally random or not.
As far as bullet sponging goes, yes it can be a problem, but mostly to poorly explained mechanics. Related is TB's point about aim down sites being unnecessiary, it works great with charged shot weapons to deal an opening head shot, or if you can create distance, and take a lot out of some of the more tanky enimies. Personally what bothers me more is the elemental effects on foot soldiers (toxic cloud yakuza etc) makes sense for some of the monsters and other mobs but would be nice if those enemy mods where a little more tailored by enemy type. Otherwise using the right kind of weapon will let you take down an enemy that would otherwise take for ever. I defenitley can get into a 'shooter flow' and keep momentum up.
TL;DR:
Great game with minor issues that may be big issues for some. If you must min/max all the time some poor design choices with loot may have you breaking up all flow in the game. It is apparent this was made by a studio without much experience in arpgs and looters, but it is by no means totally broken, much of the problems are definately patchable. More importantly the game looks good and core sword and gun play is well animated and responsive. If you hate looter shooters enough that it will distract you from the really solid FPS then maybe skip this one.

I'm normaly too lazy to bother to write a review for a game... But I'll make an exception.
Shovel Knight is easily one of the best games I've ever played, and no doubt, my favorite platformer. It manages to make a perfect mix of engaging, fun mechanics, challenging difficulty that values actual skill above anything else, a nostalgic, but at the same time modern look, an amazing soundtrack and a sprinkle of simple, good humor.

Plague of Shadows was an absolute rework of the game. It kept the same world, with a story that, while not breaking the main one, was still very engaging and a joy to follow; most importantly, though, it brought a whole new set of mechanics, changing gameplay to something not just different to the main game, but also just as original as Shovel Knight itself had been before. I had paid for 1 good quality game, and received 2 games I dare call masterpieces.
And now Specter of Torment came out, and with just what I have played of it so far, I'll have to correct my previous statement. I received not 2, but 3 masterful games, with a fourth one on the way!
This isn't a game that you'll just play, have some fun with, and then just forget about. This is a game you can, and will, thoroughly enjoy.

This game's alright... I'm not at all alright while playing it, but I still love it. After the rage wears off, the game gives you a good sense of accomplishment when you finally get that 0 fault gold medal run, especially on later (hard) stages.
While Trials Fusion is a streamlined trials game (it is much, much easier than Evolution), there is still a good amount of hard tracks in the base game, and a few of them only the most persistent players will be able to "gold medal" (while others will rage quit out of the game and write a review...). There are 8 zones in the base game, and each one has 6 to 10 tracks in it (8 on average), that number is significantly increased with the season pass, which adds 6 new zones. Right now, 9/10/2014, the season pass only offers 3 zones, with 3 more on the way before May 2015. The game also includes a track editor, so you can create your own tracks, and you can easily access and play tracks built by other people online (which are pretty impressive from what I've seen/played).
Now I'm not a big fan of Ubisoft's PC releases, because I usually get hit by poor optimization issues that plague a lot of their games at release, this game's performance however, pleasantly surprised me and put a big fat smile on my face, after the stutter fest that was Trials Evolution Gold Edition, I wasn't very hopeful going into this one. The game runs perfectly smooth maxed out on my machine, and the only stutter I got was on a graphically intensive track, while I had 2 video streams running in the background, after trying the same track without flash videos hogging my cpu, the stutter went away, and the game ran buttery smooth again.
For reference, my PC specs are:
i7 920 @3Ghz
gtx660ti 2gb
8gb ram
win7 64bit
It's worth mentioning that the game has a pretty good, yet weird sense of humor, for example whenever you finish a track, something funny and dumb is sure to happen, like the rider falling of his bike after he crosses the finish line, landing in the water and racing a cruise ship, or when you cross a finish line that's on top of a 2 story hut, the door closes behind you, and the hut starts flying off like a rocket. I also really enjoy the AI commentary (I guess you can call them the narrators), and the biker's yells and woohoos remind me of Homer Simpson.
This game is a steal even at full price, and on a decent sale it should be a no-brainer if you played and liked previous Trials games, but I'm sure 2D platformer game enthusiasts would love it as well. As for the score, I'm giving it a 9/10.
