I don't like RPG maker games.  I don't like the fact that so many of them have some ideas, but just get lazy and use the cookie cutter sprites, environments and even battle scenarios.  It bores me to tears.
Arafell has the one thing so many RPG maker games seem to lack, in my opinion.  Identity.  The game is not perfect by any means, but if you can forgive a battle system that isn't terribly showy, it's a fun adventure.  I've only just started, but the writing is good.  It's not an immersive game, but it is self aware, funny, and likes to play with the tropes of the genre.  I'm also a sucker for worlds set in floating islands.  If there are any recycled assets from a cookie cutter spread sheet, I'd be hard pressed to find them here, as every character, even nameless ones, have a portrait for talking, fairly distinct sprites, and even a little portrait animation here and there.
The game is lacking a bit in the showiness as battles aren't slow, but the character animation seems to be a bit sluggish and without pizazz.  Also, no battle music except for bosses.  It's a bit jarring to fight moon cats while the same peaceful choral forest theme plays in the background that loops over and over again.  Good thing the music itself is good.
Arafell is a game I recommend as someone who loves JRPGs, but not RPGmaker games.  It's got pretty good writing, a beautiful world to explore, and some nice modern conveniences like showing you where quest items go, warning you before entering areas and giving you save reminders, and teleport gates.  While not immersive, these are nice quality of life conveniences and I do think they are worthwhile.
Worth a look.  It lacks flash, but has plenty of substance.

If anyone out there ever played Sid Meier's Gettysburg and loved it then youre in for a treat with this game, as Ultimate General Gettysburg seems to be a clone of one of Sed Meier greatest games.
With that said if you are not familire with Sid Meier's Gettysburg, the game is rudimetery RTS where you pick your side, North or South and are then given a set number of units to command over the three day Battle of Gettysburg. Your actions will determin unit size throughout the battle and eventully determine the entire outcome of the compaign.
Outside the nastagia aspect, the game is pretty average. The graphics aren't 8-bit basic, but they aren't push your GPU to the limits awesome. The creaters seem to really just be shooting for a remake of the original SM's Gettysburg.There is no real story outside of you changing the outcome of the battel with how you play, and the soundtrack is almost nonexistance.However, this was the same with the original SM's Gettysburg so this really does not really detract from the game.
What does however take from the game is its controls. Orders are given by selecting units and draging them to where you would like them just like any RTS. However in Ultimate General Gettysburg, this draws a movement line on the map as you drag it. If you mess up with your initial drag then correcting while still dragging will send your units marching in loopty loops across the  battle field while taking enemy fire. The only way to correct this is by selecting the unit again and dragging it again to reissue the command. This is minor aanoyence is magnified when you make this mistake with a whole group of units.
With it's over simplisity and handful of flaws aside, Ultimate General Gettysburg was not a half bad game. Ultimate General Gettysburg may not be one for the Hardcore RTSer, but it is definatly something to be picked up for the casual gammer, or for the those of you wishing to relive your SM's Gettysburg glory days.

This is a charming game, however there are a few issues that are a bit breaking and after seeing that it costs 6.99€ just makes me say DO NOT BUY IT. If you do find it in a bundle however (like I did) sure, get it.
Now it's time for an explanation. The game is cute and your character actually walks around "real" objects, as in, the scenes were filmed with a real camera and then blended into the game.
It's a point and click puzzle game and it isn't an easy one either. Which, again, in itself is fine.
The puzzles are usually either a bit easy to solve or at least to figure out what to do, but there's 1 of them that is really quite horribly difficult to even make sense out of it.
SPOILER about that "tip" for that puzzle, it's a page of a book with the "ONE" in "GRAMAPHONE" underlined, and a #9 on the corner of the page... what this supposedly means is, there's 9 numbers you need (for a locker with 3 digits, therefore 3 sets) and it starts with ONE, then you have to read the text and find either the actuall number like "fig. 2" being the "2" the second number you need, and then "three"... then there's a year, 1887, the "1" is the last number of the second set of numbers and "887" the last one.
The problem with this is, the game gives you NO CLUE what this book is related to or even what to look for, your character only says "A book grandpa's been reading, he wrote something on it" and that's it, you really need a guide or an epiphany to figure it out.
Lastly, and this is what made me say NO about buying this for 6,99€ is that the game... only lasted me a few minutes, seriously, there are like 5 different screens (not counting small camera transitions) and only a dozen of puzzles or so, it's a cute short "story" but it's not even an apetizer, sure, in the end it says "end of lume part 1", but it's a part where you pay 6,99€ to get.
TL;DR
- One of the puzzles is nearly impossible to solve on your own, and crucial to finish the game;
- Even if you get stuck a lot, you can beat the game in only a few minutes, not even 1 hour.
Would I recommend playing this game? Sure, it is a bit fun at most and challenging, you will probably need a guide for 1 or 2 puzzles though and it's an interesting new concept.
Would I recommend buying this game? No, unless you're either filthy rich, or get it with a bundle, seriously.
In terms of the overall game and enjoyability I give it a... maybe 8/10 (without my puzzle issue).
In terms of the price/quality ratio I give it a 1/10 just because it's visually pleasing and new.
Thanks for reading this (if anyone ever does).

Did I mention that the reinforcements you receive appear from off-map in real-time, as they did historically? Because that's another thing that propels the battle onwards. New units are your resources.

Ultimate General: Gettysburg is an awesome game. For those who want an American Civil War (ACW) stratagy game, here it is.
The game is centered around the battle of Gettysburg July 1-3(4) 1863. In the main mode (Main Menu-Start new battle) you can fight the battle of Gettysburg as the Union or Confederacy, and choose your opponent AI (9 types of AI: Adds a lot to replay value). The battle is fought in Scenarios, each one being triggered one after the other depending on what you accomplished in the last one you fought. There are more scenarios than I can count honestly. You keep fighting through scenario's untill you fully defeat the enemy, of you run out of time. You can also end up fighting battles on July 4, which is interesting because this never happend in history. All of the possible scenarios are playable in the "Custom battle" section of the main menu. Multiplayer is also fun to do, but there are not nearly as many scenario's as there are in single player, which can be good or bad, depending on your view point. But here is a list of pro's and con's.
Pros: Helpful and thorough tutorial videos.
Combat is easy to learn and master.
Brigades are historically numbered.
Corps and Brigades have historical commanders (Archer,Pender,John Reynolds, Richard S. Ewell, Ect.)
Artillery has been fixed with the hotfixes.
Art. is ballanced so it isn't devestating with casualties, but does lots of morale damage.
Good map design and elevation.
TONS of replay value with harder AI and (probably) over 30 scenarios.
Multiplayer-compatible
No scenario is completley impossible.

CONS: All units look the same (Iron bridage doesn't wear black hats)
No steam workshop
Artillery can sometimes not fire even though they are looking over a field from a hill.
The "Texas brigade", supposedly one of the best southern brigades, has terrible morale.
Game can freeze (this issue is being dealt with by developers)
Reinforcements will come earlier for the enemy than they will when you play as them.
NOTE: I personally think that it would have been better to include more battles in this game, like Antietam, Second Manasas, Shiloh, ect. If not that, at least a map/battle editor so we could make those battles. A steam workshop would also be really nice.
OVERALL: 9.5/10. Awesome game. Would definatly reccomend it for people if they asked. I wish these people would make more games like this, so here are some ideas. Ultimate General: Waterloo, Ultimate General: The American Civil War, Ultimate General: Napoleon (battles of Napoleonic era). And why stop there? The possibilities are endless.
EDIT: +1.5 for the addition of Night battles and artillery limbering.

Just to begin with: Arma 3 is my first game of the entire Arma Series. So please don't expect any comparison or stuff like that to Arma 2 or older titles. Right now i have 1,5k hours played in Arma 3 so time to sum things up:
So, do i recommend this game? It depends on your playstyle. If you're into teamplay, Milsim, long scenarios and you have alot of creativity thats your game of choice. But let's see some classic pros and cons.
Pros:
*Mods: there is an enourmus variability of mods in Arma, thanks to the developers how activly encourage the community to participate. If the vanilla game isn't enough for you in terms of weapons, factions, vehicles or scenarios there are plenty of awesome mods out there to fulfill your desires.
*Editor/ Zeus: Arma is perfect for creating your own operations or missions. And especially with the Zeus-Module you can adjust your mission in real time to events happening. So its really hard to get bored in Arma.
*Content: in most games, purchasing DLCs means spending (alot of) money on something that doesn't necessarly develop the game in a good way. But in Arma every DLC so far introduced new features and improvements. And the best thing: if you don't wanna buy any DLCs, most platform updates/ improvements are available for non-premium users.
So those are the main positive aspects i want to mention, let's talk about the rather negative points...
*Complexibilty: Arma is NOT an easy game to learn (i quote a friend of mine: "It's not a  run & gun game" [Hydrox] and i have to admit, Arma 3 was the first game to almost make me smash my keyboard out of frustration. After killing of dozens of attackers, disabeling tanks and shooting down helicopter gunships, you might still be killed by the lone rifleman hiding in a bush. And one more thing: there are loads of stuff to remember. So expect to be investing some time.
*Hardware: Be prepared to run this game at 25 to 35 FPS if you don't have a powerfull rig. I'm running it at medium to high settings and getting 30+ FPS. Recent patches improved alot here.
My personal opinion: Arma is my most played game so far and i had moments so epic, funny or unreal they still get told while having a beer with my friends. (Sidenote: One involves an unintentional parachute jump from a boat... and without a parachute xD). I'm really looking forward for the further development of this game.

Holy hell, this is one fantastic game! If Borderlands, Doom and Diablo had a baby, it would be named Shadow Warrior 2. I have yet to find something I dislike about the game. I literally beat the first Shadow Warrior (not the original) the night before 2 came out, and I have to say that the controls are faaaarrrrr more refined and intuitive. I really like the upgrade system, weapon mod system, and just how good it feels to slice and dice one second and blow things up the next. It's seriously a fantastic game so far, even the fight music and main menu music is amazing, super fitting to the overall feel of the game. The banter between some of the characters is pretty great, cheesy and funny. It's like Borderlands where you're free to roam around in individual areas, so it's not really "open world" but it's open enough, and procedurally generated enough to make going back to a location feel fresh. Speaking of going back, there's a teleport system that allows you to teleport back to your base, so you can sell stuff or whatever, and then you can teleport back to EXACTLY where you teleported from. It's fantastic, no running back and forth between locations, it's just simple and streamlined and very well thought out.
I won't go into all the minute details of the game so as to avoid spoilers, suffice it to say I'm loving it so far, and it may in fact be me 2016 Game of the Year.

This game is probably one of the best platformers I've ever played.
Shovel Knight plays in a similar way to a Megaman game, where you have to defeat all the knights of the order of no quarter (kind of like the robot masters in Megaman), and the levels are composed of "rooms".
The level design is so well made, it teaches you brilliantly the mechanics of the game really quickly, and there are very few moments where you say to yourself "this is the game's fault", because usually every death is justified, the mechanics in one room were taught to you before hand so you know what to expect.
The Plague of Shadows update gives you (once you've cleared the game) the possibility to play as Plague Knight, one of the Knights of the Order of no quarter. The gameplay changes entirely, and you get to replay the entire game as a baddie. It's really fun and is a great addition to the game.
The story, while being simple, is pretty good in my opinion. You are Shovel Knight, an adventurer that used to roam the land with his partner, Shield Knight. They go exploring the Tower of Fate, where Shield Knight gets defeated and Shovel Knight is forced to escape. He then retires to a more peaceful life, but The Enchantress and her Order of no quarter start ruling the land. Shovel Knight, wanting to fight this evil, comes back and begins his quest to defeat The Enchantress.
In the update, Plague Knight's quest is to brew a potion that will make him extremely powerful, but for that he will need the essence of every Knight of the Order of no Quarter, including The Enchantress' essence. With the help of Mona, your alchemist assistant, you begin your quest to defeat every knight and brew this strength potion.
The OST. Oh man the OST. It is composed by the man, the legend, Jake Kaufman, and he just nails it once again. The soundtrack is really good and fits the overall feeling of the game extremely well. I don't think that Jake Kaufman could ever fail the soundtrack for a game. The soundtrack of Plague of Shadows is just as good.
I greatly recommend buying Shovel Knight. While it is not the longest game, it is still extremely fun to play and definitely worth it's price, the level design is incredibly well done, the controls feel really well, the OST is insanely good. Yacht Games' first title is a masterpiece.

Granted.. This is all from only 2 hours of actually playing.
I played the single player up to the first couple missions so I could play in co-op, and everything seemed fine. It felt like more of the Shadow Warrior I played back in 2013, but when I first started the combat things felt..... Different. In a bad way. When i first saw those health bars for enemies on the top of my screen, and felt my frames start to drop (Not by much, maybe dipping around 40-50 fps) I started to feel kind of cautious about what I got myself into.
But that was nothing until I got into co-op with a friend.
The missions are collect-a-thons in decently sized maps, at least as far as we got to. Hopefully they get better further in.
Story is just as.. 'unique' as the 2013 game, but it feels like a few steps in the wrong direction. Not to mention the scenes are just jolty and jerky as all hell. One minute you'll be talking to someone in a nicely decorated mansion, and the next second, you'll be in an extremely different and neon city. It was distracting to say the least.
Bullet sponge enemies that refuse to die. If you compare these enemies to enemies in games like Borderlands, that game was NEVER this bad. It felt like I was using nerf guns and trying to slash at enemies with a wet noodle instead of a sword.
Not to mention the enemies will randomly shove you around while you try and slash at them. The hitboxes don't make sense, and if you're trying to fight on an incline good luck. Stairs remain the hardest boss in video games.
But the WORST part is that once we started fighting in a co-op game, my frame rate CHUGGED. Like in the 10-20 range, and being constantly shoves around by the walking bullet sponges the game has as enemies, I was pushed through the ground! Falling down below the map and having to kill myself to get out.
Anyway.. Maybe the game is great and I just didn't get to the good part.

Lacks polish on every corner unfortunately. Yes this is an early access title and yes EA can have bugs. That's not what i'm talking about.
The overall concept of the game is great.
The balancing and core ideas of the game are great too. It's very clever above all how the progression in survival works and forces you to preserve materials on every corner even after a couple of hours.
But just about every core feature that's in the game feels irky / buggy to work with:
- Right click accidentally with your building gun on any machine and it will deconstruct Losing ressources that were in it and generally being a nuisance.
- The whole interface is very problematic, disappearing cursor, unintuitive controls, buttons that dont work as they should. Nothing gamebreaking, you eventually learn how to work around them. Inconsistent use overall. (Some things require "e" to charge them, some need to be opened first for instance...) Annoying nevertheless.
- The Energy and Transport system are cool but very annoying to work with. Moving a line one block lower because you misjudged something and built it a bit off, good luck with that, will cost you a ♥♥♥♥♥on of ressources and a blob of interconnecting logisticshoppers.
- Energytransfer. We have lasers that transfer power over 64 blocks but no cables that distribute power to something 2 blocks away. Instead you have to kinda misuse batteries to connect things. I suspect it's because of the 1 block 1thing development philosophy that this game went for. In the early days of Industrialcraft over at Minecraft they used cables that measured 1 x 1meter... not a perfect solution but at least you had something to work with. If there is anything in the techtree then it's way to far down. (Solar panels before basic cables ? Really ?)
- The energy grid is very simplistic and lacks complexity once you see through it. It's just batteries / machines that have energy, or they dont now distribute evenly with limited tools.
- Combat... should have left it out, it just looks really bad and unfinished and doesnt add anything to the game.
- Once you have a bigger base you need some sort of navigating tools so you can dig straight tunnels to where you need them because the game is seriously annoying if you have to build 2-3 blocks to connect things. The game has a holomap for that and a map that is very confusing to use and needs alot of time to get used to. Simple coordinates on the scanner would have solved this problem entirely, but no, we have a bloated graphics effect.
- Death doesnt mean anything. It just ports you back with ALL ressources. Take the survival aspect out of it if death is meaningless.
- Unnecessary robots flying around in your face, and the spiderbot. Have fun with the spiderbot, it doesnt do anything except block your view in your base day in and day out.
- The Scanner doesnt work proper. While the scanner is cool if you scroll the mousewheel once up or down you see that the thing is buggy. Pretty much sums up how such an easy spottable bug got past the Dev or that he didn't care about it.
- Graphics are somewhat dated. Not a huge thing.
- The name... has nothing to do with fortresses, should have named it Factorycraft or something.
- Multiplayer is very buggy. The dev is not capable of reproducing alot of the reported issues. We could reproduce them on every single client in the first try. Well... yeah.
- Ore distribution is really cool and works better than in minecraft as it forces you to branch out the base naturally and think of ways to make things easier.
- The Scanner is cool.
- Energysystem of your suit forces you to be carefull about your ressources.
- Progression is really smart and fun. You can't just step away 10 hours and then have a ♥♥♥♥♥on of ressources, the limited automated storages make sure of that.
I get the feeling that whoever programmed this is potentially a great game designer but shouldn't be the person who pushes out any releases. Have someone that does quality control and treat this as a conceptual prototype. The game lacks an overall control / ui concept and now wants to leave Early Access.

I have always loved strategy and tactical games, more turn based rather than RTS but this game brings me closer back to the RTS fold.  I really like this game, especially in multiplayer battles.
Good things about this game:
If you like civil war era type games or napoleonic type combats this game will likely appeal to you.  The map is beautifully crafted and you can see vast amounts of soldiers moving around following your orders or littering the battlefield with their corpses.   All orders given are represented on the game map in the form of movement arrows  and in true civil war combat style positioning of your units, using cover and taking advantage of the high ground are an essential part of your strategy.
The game also only costs $15 and if you don't like multiplayer it's a fun single player experience.
Bad things about this game:
The multiplayer match finding interface is bad.  Finding games can be difficult without having one of your steam friends join.  I have added some players that I did manage to play against and can now play these guys when available however.
You can setup your own multiplayer game which then allows others in the game lobby to connect to you but there usually aren't many people waiting there so you have to hope that someone will eventually join you.
That's it - the multiplayer match finder sucks but the game is good.

Lume, tai yra mažas "point-and-click" nuotykių žaidimas, kuriame jūs valdote anūką, kurio užduotis senelio namuose atstatyti elektros energija. Žaidimas yra šviesus ir linksmas. Jis turi neįprastą, bet gražią vizualinę pusę kuri šiam žaidimui suteikia savotiškumo. Jei jums patiko tokie žaidimai, kaip Machinarium ar Botanicula jums be abejonės patiks ir šis žaidimas.
Žaidime atvykstame aplankyti senai matytą senelį, bet mes jo nerandame namuose, o vietoj jo tik raštelį. Perskaitę raštelį sužinome, kad senelis susidūrė su elektros tiekimo problemomis, todėl nutarė pats išsiaiškinti kas nutiko. Ir tuo pačiu paliko mums pūzlęs(jų yra ~7) kurių pagalba, galėsime padėti seneliui. Ir nieko nedelsdami puolame ieškoti užuominų, bei spręsti užduotis!
Vis dar galvojate, ką po velnių reiškia mano pasisakymas "Paprastumo grožis" ? Norint suprasti šį teiginį, grįžkime prie vizualinės žaidimo pusės. Žaidimas sukurtas iš popieriaus tikrąją tą žodžio prasme, žaidimo išvaizdos kūrimui buvo panaudotos popierinės konstrukcijos su šiek tiek kompiuterinės grafikos. O aplinkų perėjimai yra tiesiog nufilmuoti su vaizdo kamera, taigi tai yra labai paprasta bet ir tuo pačiu gražu ar ne ?
Kad ir kaip būtų viskas gražu ir linksmą, žaidimas turi ir minusų. Tai yra istorijos ilgis, jis siekia vos 1h, tai gi visas žaidimo malonumas ir smagi atmosfera greitai išblėsta. Kaip be būtų, tai nereiškia kad žaidimas yra prastas, jis tikrai malonus ir linksmas, Žinant, kad žaidimo kaina siekia vos 5LT, jo trukmė tampa nebe tokia svarbi. Kurėjų teigimu šis žaidimas yra tik pirmoji dalis didelės istorijos, taigi belieka tikėtis, kad Lume antroji dalis bus ilgesnė :)

Oh the fun time building bridges so people can safely continue their travels. The trial and error it takes as you continue to test which parts work and which parts break under the pressure. Does each element work out for the better or will it cause people to die? And more importantly, will these vehicles be able to go through these portals?
When looking for a puzzle game that will test your mind constantly, you can’t go wrong with bridge construction games. With Bridge Construction Portal, this does not deviate with testing the mind. With the levels starting out easy to get the hang of things, each bridge jumps in difficulty throughout all 60 levels. The only difference between this and other bridge building games is the inclusion of Portal as instead of building a bridge that looks like everyday people would use when they travel, you’re in testing chambers. And instead of empty vehicles...well there may be people on them.
Unlike other bridge building games, this is a little bit more relaxed. You don’t have to worry about moving bridge parts, well unless the bridge is swinging, you know how much money you spent but you’re not on a budget, you can just have one vehicle go to the finish to continue, and having a bridge piece break is no big deal. The challenge comes from the Portal objects and if you want to do convoys. Don’t worry about the people on the vehicles, that would be ridiculous, the vehicles only need to be there to count. You might want to invest in some security though as you will be cited as killing them and someone might enact revenge.
Depending on the level, it can contain turrets, companion cubes, gel, energy orbs, or a combination of these along with portals which occur in most levels. When the turrets get sight of a vehicle, it will start to shoot at it, so be sure to find out a way to destroy it so you can succeed. Companion cubes are usually used to press buttons the vehicles won’t be able to hit, but can be also used as bullet shields and to destroy turrets. There is also the inclusion of bouncy and speed gel on the track which can help with the portals as the speed hurdles them through the bridge. Lastly, and more annoyingly, there are energy orbs which need to go into their sockets, which act as the buttons, but you need to bounce them off of roads to do it. Which can lead to a lot of adjusting so the timing can be just right.
You only need to bring one vehicle, or in some levels one set, through a bridge to be able to continue. But if you want more challenge, you can choose to do a convoy. A convoy can range from 3 vehicles to 16 vehicles that can be on the bridge at the same time, so if the bridge can stand one, it might not stand to a convoy. It gets even harder on the levels that require multiple lanes or vehicle timing. If there are energy orbs or companion cubes that can get in the way, be sure to account for that too as they will get in the way as well.
WIth Portal being in the design’s forefront, I was not disappointed. The menu screen is nicely done, with objects being added to it with every level, as you are set as a worker. Each level is treated as a test chamber, with the level card being the same as it would be if it was in a Portal game, and Glados making an appearance to help you out and give you information about the facility. However, Glados does stop talking to you for long periods of time so if you like Glados you will be wishing for more and if you don’t wish the silence was for the whole game. And adding the fact that in the test chambers, the vehicles have three people, two of which can comically fall off and out of the test chamber as they undoubtedly wish they called in sick.
Most of the things I wished this game had comes from my experience in PolyBridge. This desperately needed a fast forward button as there are quite a few long levels that do need a lot of tweaking depending on what elements are there. Having a fast forward button would definitely help in times where you just need to see if one element is working out without having to wait long. I also wished that there was a click drag select, and with this a copy paste, as this helps a lot as symmetry is the key and if you mess up on a whole area you can delete everything rather than having to select pieces or connectors one by one. You do also get an undo button but no redo button so if you end up undoing too much, you won’t be able to take it back.
On top of that, it has problems of its own. The vehicles can and will glitch out and cause the back wheel to go under (through?) the bridge piece and cause you to slightly adjust it. While it might seem that it was because it might have been a little bit too high at first, it dawns on you during a convoy when only one vehicle gets glitched and all the others are fine. There were also instances where objects fell differently without the player doing anything to change it as well. In one of the later levels, a companion cube has to hit turrets and when it does it tilts so it can’t get stuck on the platform. In that level I had those objects hit differently three times, one of which caused a turrent to hit the next one thus causing the cube tobe stuck on the platform, till it decided to fall correctly.
I have to say that despite the frustration that came with the glitching wheels and randomness, I did have fun building bridges in this Portal styled bridge construction game. As I never played the original Bridge Constructor game, nor its spinoffs, my experience in PolyBridge and their features that made it easier on the player was in Bridge Constructor Portal. With the leniency on your budget, this might be the more relaxed version as you only need to get the vehicles to the finish. So if you like bridge building and don’t mind the drawbacks it has, go for it. But if you know you don’t like games like PolyBridge, and really only getting it because it holds the Portal name, you won’t like this one.

Bridge Constructor Portal takes the physics mechanics from Bridge Constructor and blends them with the puzzle mechanics from Valve’s famous Portal. With GLaDOS as our instructor and set in the delightfully familiar Aperture Testing Labs, it’s a delightful nod to a much loved series.
In Bridge Constructor we are given the task of getting our cargo from point A to B by building a bridge. We also have drivers and some helpers but don’t worry about them. Squish them to your hearts content. It uses precise physics mechanics with a combination of scaffolding and wires, so this game will be a lot easier for those with an understanding of building principles. As an engineer, my husband scoffed at my pathetic attempts to solve the game and kept yelling at me that I wasn’t building it structurally sound. Nonetheless, you can find a solution even if you have no background in this area, but it won’t always be pretty, so don’t show it to any professionals. I must admit I had the most fun when my cars flipped out 6 times and eventually spun and pushed each other over the victory line.
If you’ve played Portal, the portal mechanics will be familiar to you. Coloured portals teleport you from A to B, companion cubes and buttons abound, goo can accelerate you or provide a trampoline-type surface whilst turrets will shoot you if you enter their line of sight. If you’ve not played Portal, I command you to go do so immediately.
Now try to get that precious cargo from A to B, by building a bridge whilst being shot by lasers, having to navigate portals, fall from great heights, bounce off surfaces and accelerate quickly and you’ll see that the challenge (and fun!) level has just been upped. As the levels (60 in total) progress, all the mechanics come into play and things get a little bit crazy. GLaDOS (voiced by original voice actor Ellen McLain) will give you droll, emotionless statements to motivate you forward in true Portal fashion. The writing and humour aren’t quite there for me although I appreciated the attempt.
It has two victory conditions – a single success, which is usually fairly easily obtainable even if the entire bridge comes crashing down behind you, and the convoy. The convoy is when a whole series of trucks need to make the journey without being dropped in a vat of acid or ending up in a 6 car pileup. This means the bridge has to be firmly structurally sound and able to take the weight & load of multiple cars and crossovers need to take place without a mid-air collision. Much harder! The dual options offer a fun and light way to complete a level, and a more serious success route. If you’re frustrated you can move on and go back to your convoy later with level select and it’s akin to playing it on easy or hard mode.
For those with no clue how to build a bridge, you do get a handbook that explains some basic principles of load, pressure, and design and then you’ll need to equip the old brain and get cracking. You’re not timed and you get an unlimited amount of attempts, including test runs, so even on the higher difficulty levels, there’s no real pressure and you can try as many things as you fancy which makes it a fairly relaxing experience.
It doesn’t have a storyline and it’s not quite the epic journey that the original Portal series was, so for those hoping for a little bit of Portal 3, this definitely isn’t it. I’d also hoped for the ability to place portals yourself, but unfortunately, these are all static. But despite these few disappointments, I found myself really charmed by each new challenge and pumping the air in victory when my convoy made it. If you enjoy the construction mechanics of Bridge Constructor, the Portal elements add some unique and interesting puzzles that in my opinion are much enhanced on the original game. It’s simple and intuitive, a fun little game with a little bit of tech, a dollop of puzzle and a cup of crazy thrown in.

After almost 500 hours, this is still the game that I always go back to. It's the first PC game I've ever played, and there's a good reason that it's still going 10 years after its initial release. This is how a free to play game should be.
You start off with all the weapons you need. There are many weapons, but in most cases the stock weapons are the most reliable. There's no piece of equipment that will give you a direct upgrade: weapons that increase your speed will make you more vulnerable to damage for example. Knowing how to play is the only way to do well.
The game is still getting major updates with new maps, new weapons and new game modes. It has a huge community, and I've never had trouble queing for a match, and the games are fast-paced and unpredictable.
Finally there's the cosmetic items. They don't do anything in terms of gameplay, but if you play long enough you'll end up buying a few. It's really just a donation to the development team, and if nothing else a guy with a candy-cane rocket launcher and a tall hat looks pretty interesting.

Greetings Everyone!  Today I’ll be reviewing “Etherium” an interesting RTS that seems to have had a rocky start.  I purchased this game quite a bit ago and had to request a refund due to technical issues (the game crashed at the end of every battle) and I’m back now to give a round two attempt.  So, is the game any good?  Did they fix the crash issue I had?
My Eyes:   Let’s start with some cosmetics; the game immediately feels a generation behind.  Why?  Outside of the opening cinematic there is very little voice overs, each faction (and sub faction) has its own voice over but they are extremely limited, the faction I played, the humans, only had two differences and that was a male and female voice.  To be honest the sound effects and voice overs were so bland that I found myself muting the game after an hour or so of play.  The graphics are also ‘last gen’ not up to scale with the big games out there.  Some of the levels seem to have issues with their shaders causing levels to be so bright it is hard to see what’s going on; others using colors that cause units to almost blend in.
Ready for Orders:  Mechanically we have a solid RTS that is enjoyable but again feels a generation behind.  This game is in dire need of some QOL (Quality of Life) improvements.  After playing the likes of StarCraft, Sins, and Dawn of War I expect to be able to queue stuff up, but I can’t.  The game focuses on territories that are captured for both defensive needs and resources.   The turrets you can build are a bit over the tope early game which leads to a design choice that makes early game ‘land grabs’ the way to go.  Units have characteristics that give it passive abilities like being able to hide in forests or being airborne.  This is a great way for people to identify units and understand their function immediately.  The game also has a slower pace of game as the units themselves move slow by modern RTS and things die slowly if not directly countered.
We’ve seen this before:  Let me say that this is a solid RTS, with ‘okay’ graphics and sounds but the game feels like it is missing a soul, the units are simple and bland in a rock paper scissors kind of way.  There is a conquest mode (which is to be fair the only real thing to do as the community seems a bit dead) which has some interesting ideas but becomes a bit grindy no matter how well you are doing.  Expect to fight battles that your opponent has no chance of winning but you are forced to play anyway.  This brings me to the biggest annoyance of the game.  Yes, the game crashing bug.   The game played fine for a few hours then started having the original bug I experienced.  With this being the problem there is little I can do to progress as even after a reinstall the game still won’t play.
Ultimately, I won’t mince words here; I cannot recommend a game that won’t reliably play.  The second time I bought this game was during the recent sale for $1.99 and I actually feel like I was a bad sale as it felt robbed of my time.  The game is really not worth recommending even if it worked fine but the crash bug (that many seem to have) creates not only an unplayable game but a game I was invested well into a conquest that I will now never complete.  I’d stay way for no other reason than that.

This is a giant step backwards from the first (excellent) Shadow Warrior re-boot.  The graphics have not improved.  This game looks identical to the first one.  The levels are randomly generated, and as such, they kind of become "samey" and boring.  There are no giant or interesting bosses (7 hours in).  There's no pacing.  It's just a basic basic basic FPS map, and you go from point A to point B following a golden trail of bread crumbs on the mini map., and fight the same 10 enemies over and over and over again.  And then you teleport to the hub world to get your next mission.  A hub world.  We are FAR beyond this in 2016.  It's hilariously dated.
The procedural generation of the maps just doesn't do any favorrs for this type of game.  It's awkward where the last game was tight.  It's dull where the last game was a series of set pieces.  Every change between the last title and this one is a mis-step.
They added a TON of new weapons.  But at the end of the day, all the melee weapon are functionally identical, so it doesn't really add a lot to the experience.  You can grind for weapon upgrades, but the combat is so boring and repetitive that you won't want to.
The story  is unremarkable. You have another character in your head (like the demon in the first game), but the charm isn't there.   I'd recommend buying the first Shadow Warrior reboot.  This sequel feels like a slog.  I'm incredibly bummed out that the developers went sideways instead of moving forwards.  I can't recomment purchasing.

- Most of the game is about setting up a mining operation and get the necessary resources/ores to finally build the stuff you need to leave the planet (game end)
- Mobs / Tower defence mode has been introduced: so while building/exploring the alien planet you also need to fight and/or setup defences depending on how much you get noticed by the local aliens
- There are "Hive Minds"! O_o
- If you like crafting and building automated stuff this is the game for you!
- This is mainly a single player game IMO but they put in a multiplayer mode too (I don't use it) which is a bit awkward to setup, but they're still improving it
So basically my tip is to go buy it!

It only shows about 2 hours on my playtime on steam because I finished the game on my ps3.  Darksiders is, to put it in the simplest terms, a mix between Zelda (think Ocarina of Time combat and puzzles), and Devil May Cry (think combat with the combo  system).  Although Darksiders bring nothing new or revolutionary in its gameplay, it implements and executes the genre it borrows from exceptionally well.  The puzzles are clever and never overwhelming difficult, while the combat feels tight and exciting.
One thing that deserves praise for this game is its artstyle and design, and the overall world it creates.  The artstyle is heavily influenced by comics, and I like the art in the game and its character designs as much as comics such as Spawn.  The level design is also exceptional, and the maps never lead you in circles if you follow through, though backtracking is sometimes necessarily, though not used to a drag.  Weapon and moves upgrades keep gameplay exciting and gives combat a sense of progression.

Overall, this is a very polished action game with great design and stylish art.  Nothing too novel, yet all elements come together extremely well.  If a post-apocalypitc  world with the four horsemen trapped between a war between angels and demons sounds appealing to you, this game will keep you satisfied until the very end.  The identity of the game, instead of coming from novelly implemented elements or a trademark idea (or gimmick, if it's just a cheap hook), comes from its world and its artstyle and character designs.  The difficulty is just right.  Bosses are fun and challenging, and new items and weapons open up the map pretty nicely.  You also get to ride a horse, which feels really nice and convenient for travelling.  One thing I highly recommend is playing this game with a gamepad.  Solid buy.  I bought this game twice, once on steam and once on ps3.

I've heard this described as The Legend of Zelda for adults, and while I think the lines are not so rigidly drawn as that suggests, there certainly is some merit to the comparison. This does indeed play like a Zelda game, where you need to find Item A to progress to Location A, which contains item B and a doorway to Location B. Combat-wise, it's very fluid and feels like Castlevania: Lord of Shadow, Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning, or perhaps even an Arkham game, with fluid area-of-effect sword swings and lots of options for upgrading and customization.
Story-wise, I happen to love biblical mythology, and this is full of it. I may not believe in the whole hokey-pokey Jesus nonsense in my personal life, but I definitely appreciate the lore of the 4 Horsemen and their relationship with heaven and hell. You might find this to be a bit predictable and linear, but this really isn't the sort of game that depends on story to be enjoyable.
In total, it's very deserving of its metascore, and if the franchise pack goes on sale for $8 again, get it.

Darksiders is a third person spectacle brawler with heavy puzzle and some exploration elements in a semi-open world.  You play as War, Horseman of the Apocalypse and you are pretty much a total badass; slicing up demons and angels alike in a quest to clear your name in the case of who destroyed the entirety of humanity.
It has excellent dynamic brawling combat, you will have a fairly good selection of moves abilities and equipment to choose from although you are likely to settle into a few combinations of moves that are particularly effective.  A number of Boss fights are clear highlights of the game and are challenging without being so tough as to totally break the pace by killing you many times over.  The character design and voicing is top shelf and the art assets are impressive, though the texture resolutions do sometimes show being a generation behind these days.  The puzzles are mostly well designed, satisfyingly Tomb Raideresque.
The downsides are that when the open world opens up, it mainly plays as just padding getting from one place to another although this is partially mitigated by a few scattered quick travel points.   I said that you have a number of weapons and items at your disposal and that is true but the number of quick slots available is very limited, and changing to other items might be necessary during a fight, maybe that isn't true if you are using mouse and keyboard; but I couldn't tell you because otherwise the game is clearly designed with controllers in mind.  If you hate invisible walls, prepare to be annoyed by them here, and the minimap/world map are functional but could be better.  One final complaint is that I had trouble with the Steam Achievements not processing correctly at some points when you clearly should have earned them.
All told I feel that Darksiders was definitely worth the time (about 20 hours of actual play) and the cash as it can be had for a song these days.

I first played this game 11 years ago to the day, and back then, it was disheartening to see the game seemed to have been abandoned. I am thrilled that today the game is now released, streamlined and refined. It uses RM2K3 (which some idiot thinks is cheapskate - but that does not take from the charm of the game, in fact it reminds me of Secret of Mana, that's exactly the style it needs to go for). Back in the days, me and many others used this game to learn about such things as game design, creative writing etc. and here's to hope this cute little game, now one of many on a saturated indie market, inspires a new generation of devs as it inspired the last.
The characters are refined, relatable, interesting. Exposition is a little heavy-handed, with a couple of bad writing points (the archery contest is particularly cringy, as the rules seem to change as the scene goes) but it's much better than the 2007 version. The story, while I am afraid probably short or at least not much beyond the original game, is engaging. It's more of a visual novel, though it has good RPG elements to match. Obviously, the graphics is where the game shines. As far as 16bit goes this is beautiful. This game features an almost open world, too - no world map here, you literally walk from one area to the next. This amazed me as a kid, and this is still appreciated today. Now, of course the story is nothing ground breaking, but it's likable and fun, which is more than I can ask of many AAA games today.
Game design isn't too bad either, RM2K3 is far superior in this respect than RMXP/VX even with custom scripts. While there has been some effort in streamlining progression since 2005, it often feels a little hapless. Case in point : The first boss -literally- requires you to grind to reach it, though.  The first boss has an attack that can prevent you from using abilities (Thunder does that), and has a pattern you need to understand but too often you can't actually beat the pattern unless you've grinded quite a bit beyond what it says are the level requirements.
Other minor cons would involve all of the quests etc. dumped into the inventory. I understand how RM2K3 limits things, but it would be wiser to make a single journal item that keeps track of the crafting recipes, quests etc. Other RM2K3 games, such as the excellent free to play Everlong, do it.
All in all, doesn't push RM2K3 too far, but it expands on it as far as it needs to.  Beyond my nostalgia for a game that made an impact on my childhood and my excitement to see it finally be completed and put on Steam, I'm confident to say it's well worth the price tag. Enjoyable, likable, and solidly fun if you like J-RPGs. :)

The AI is also an enemy to be reckoned with. It seems that the time that devs usually spent to increase the graphics of a game so that the player can scroll down to the last detail of a single soldier (honestly, how often do we do that when playing?) in this game is wisely spent on making the AI responsive and dangerous; different AI personalities can be chosen that increase the replay value of every single scenario. For its price the game is a STRONG BUY!

If I were to describe this game in one word, that word would be "HolyCrapThisGameIsScary!".
Amnesia: The Dark Descent does not rely simply on jump scares, though there are plenty of them, instead it reels you in through it's immersive story, creepy environment, and its ability to mess with the senses. Venturing through the eerie dungeons gives you a sense of wonder and the urge to continue along the course. The game is scary but the storyline keeps pulling you back in, not allowing you to stop playing for more than a few hours.
Amnesia: The Dark Descent is special because of the fact that it does not give you great power. You can simply run and hide from any kind of creature that you encounter. You cannot fight back when being attacked, you merely die, and must come up with a way to outsmart your "opponent".  This game also affects "Daniel" the Character you are playing as. After the game carries on he begins to become insane, making it harder to perform simple tasks and in the process striking fear in your soul!
I will say that this game is not like any others before it; in fact it will inspire the Horror Survival Genre forever. This is nearly the pinnacle of Horror games because it gives the gamer a sense of curiosity and does not allow itself to be forgotten very easily in your mind.
I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys the adrenaline rush of being scared and to anyone who loves a great mysterious story.

AHEM!!
Darkness...
Silence...

the flash of a knife in the dark
I watch in horrible gut-wrenching anticipation
I tense
and then...
Pain!
PAIN AS I HAVE NEVER FELT BEFORE!
I wished with every precious milliecond of my short and inconsequential existance that the unbearable agony would cease!
when suddenly
...light
....FREEDOM
I pause... confused and exited. What is this wonderous feeling? for the first time, I wiggle my left corner... then my right... how? How is this possible? I squint around with my new found sight. At first the images make no coherent sense to me, colors and shapes swim before my eyes in a dance of choatic inanity. It seems to me that I am watching honey bear take supper with a family of badgers and a pair of rather snobish french ducklings. I see a butterfly flutter past, and my eyes follow it only to see it stop to perch on a Loaf of Bread....
...could it be?
surely my eyes must still be decieving me! but alas, as I peruse my surroundings for a second time I see nothing but a filthy kitchen with half empty bottles laying at random across the room. The counter top appeared to be overrun by a hoard of disgusting ants, and the table upon which I was laying seemed to have a Loaf of Bread sitting right in the middle, OF WHICH I WAS NOT A PART OF!
I gasped in horror
IT WASN'T TRUE!
it couldn't be!
I? Seperated from my Loaf?
I retreated within my self TRYING to regain the calm sense of quiet colaboration from which I was so violently torn!
sure enough, I could no longer regain contact with my brethren.
My soul despaired.
but I am not one to sit and loaf about in a bad situation. I gripped the surface of the table with all of my might and flung myself headlong toward the edge. I peered over, shuddering to my self at the sight of the pathogen sullied floor a few feet below. I gazed across the gap at my destination, Took a moment to steele myself for the gravity defying leap, dug my corners into the table and pushed against it with such a force that it sent me careening into the air! There was a fleeting moment of despair as I realized that I would miss my intentended target, but I quickly regained my concentration to find a solution to my predicament. As I soared past the chair between the table and countertop, I managed to just grab the top with my left corner. For a moment I thought I was safe, but as I clung to the chair, it began to tip. Slowly at first, but then faster, and FASTER! I feared it would fall to the floor and crush me beneath its weight, but in mid fall the top of the chair hit the edge of the counter top... and stayed there! This was brilliant! I hoisted myself up from my precarius perch and up to the counter top just as the last of my grip strength ran out. I lay there gasping for breath as I let my tired corners rest. But it was no more than a minute or two's respite before I was compelled to flee from the newest danger of my harrowing journey. The ants. They ran on to me climbing up my white and fluffy sides as I tried hopelessly to shake them off. I could feel my precious edibility dropping as the ants crawled up and down my quivering body. I threw myself recklessly across the counter and began to climb the huge white expanse that was the refridgerator. As I climbed I began to feel better, as the ants were shaken off and hurled to their doom at the floor below. With a sudden realization I thought to myself that maybe... just maybe, this transformation from Loaf to Slice was a good thing! I was unlike any of my kind, I could move, I could breathe, I could SEE! I COULD HEAR! As I flipped myself over the top of the fridge I spied my destiation in the distance. A small, shiny metal toaster. Though the journey was far from over I knew it would be worth it, and I had many a reason to be encouraged. I was by all means, incredible! The soul triumph of NATURE! A GOD AMONG MY PEOPLE!!! I gaze at the lands over which I WILL NO DOUBT RULE!!!! and I find comfort in the fact that ....one day! I shall rule ALL GRAINS!!! every BAGEL and BAGUETTE!!! because from this moment on I AM KING!
I... AM... BREAD!!!!
...and that's only the first level!

Just to begin with: Arma 3 is my first game of the entire Arma Series. So please don't expect any comparison or stuff like that to Arma 2 or older titles. Right now i have 1,5k hours played in Arma 3 so time to sum things up:
So, do i recommend this game? It depends on your playstyle. If you're into teamplay, Milsim, long scenarios and you have alot of creativity thats your game of choice. But let's see some classic pros and cons.
Pros:
*Mods: there is an enourmus variability of mods in Arma, thanks to the developers how activly encourage the community to participate. If the vanilla game isn't enough for you in terms of weapons, factions, vehicles or scenarios there are plenty of awesome mods out there to fulfill your desires.
*Editor/ Zeus: Arma is perfect for creating your own operations or missions. And especially with the Zeus-Module you can adjust your mission in real time to events happening. So its really hard to get bored in Arma.
*Content: in most games, purchasing DLCs means spending (alot of) money on something that doesn't necessarly develop the game in a good way. But in Arma every DLC so far introduced new features and improvements. And the best thing: if you don't wanna buy any DLCs, most platform updates/ improvements are available for non-premium users.
So those are the main positive aspects i want to mention, let's talk about the rather negative points...
*Complexibilty: Arma is NOT an easy game to learn (i quote a friend of mine: "It's not a  run & gun game" [Hydrox] and i have to admit, Arma 3 was the first game to almost make me smash my keyboard out of frustration. After killing of dozens of attackers, disabeling tanks and shooting down helicopter gunships, you might still be killed by the lone rifleman hiding in a bush. And one more thing: there are loads of stuff to remember. So expect to be investing some time.
*Hardware: Be prepared to run this game at 25 to 35 FPS if you don't have a powerfull rig. I'm running it at medium to high settings and getting 30+ FPS. Recent patches improved alot here.
My personal opinion: Arma is my most played game so far and i had moments so epic, funny or unreal they still get told while having a beer with my friends. (Sidenote: One involves an unintentional parachute jump from a boat... and without a parachute xD). I'm really looking forward for the further development of this game.

Art and style of the game - although the game has an identity crisis, not knowing if it wants to settle in 8 or 16bit era - that felt strange to me. Nontheless art is well done.
Difficulty is not well balanced - most of the time it is too easy, (e.g. too many checkpoints and bosses are too easy) I never needed to even use a single potion in the game.
The upgrade weapon/armor system and special attacks are either useless or make the game even more unbalanced and easier.
The relic system is completly unbalanced too, you will overuse the same 2-3 spells again and again because they are overpowered and ruin the game mechanics. At the same time you will rarely ever use the other 8 relics.
I didn't like the level design, most part is boring and feels like I am replaying MegaMan. Some of it feels like they ran out of original ideas and simply copied MegaMan 2.
All the secrets don't feel rewarding at all - either music notes/gold. Most of the time it is not worth the hassle of finding them because there is zero lack in gold in the game and there are special stages which reward you way too high with currency - the whole gold distrubution (e.g. from destroyed objects) is not well balanced and there is hardly any need for the upgrades because there is so little use for it due to the casual difficulty.
The challenge mode is a joke in my opinion: like 10 challenges which are way too easy, imagine a 8 year old creating levels in super mario maker, those would be more fun than these challenges. The rest of challenge mode are the old boss battles with time limits.
The final boss battle was a huge dissapointment for me, it felt like the devs got lazy.
After first completion you pretty much play the same exact boring levels, but with another hero with a new concept: moves slower, which is annoying - but has sort of a double/triple jump ability.
So for me there is no replay value after first completion- around 10 bucks for 8-9 hours of gameplay, which I did not enjoy in many aspects. Maybe this game is only marketed towards casual players. I find there are better indie options available in Steam.

I don't do many reviews, cause my grammar and spelling sucks, but I always write one, when I play a totally underated gem. You can bash me later.
I haven't played any games on RPGMaker 2k3 for the last 10 years until now. This game proves that even after 10 years, that style of RPG can be still more enjoyable than modern RPGs.
WARNING: Major Spoilers may appear after Gameplay and Music Section Review
Gameplay:
I really loved how I had a main quest and instead of following the main route, I prefered to explore the map and as many locations as possible, looted everything and did all side quests. The battle system is very nice especially in boss fights, when special events occur and you have to fight under new circumstances. Additionally, crafting system was innovative and easy to understand. I loved the puzzles, solving riddles to advance, however what I disliked was the repeated search of the keys for the next rooms or the let's go a long walk to active this button, then the whole way back and to another button the same loooong way, would have preferred more puzzles though. The auto-save reminder came helpful at the beginning, but as you progress the story it starts to get annoying, because after I've always saved, when I was expecting a boss fight, it popped up and asked me to save again. (Didn't found it to turn it off, overlooked it maybe). One of my favourite mechanics in this game and that was really something else and I have to mention and praise it, that you can f***ing crawl, swim, jump and fly! You see that rarely in a RPGMaker game with those features.
Music:
Simply wow. It had everything, calm chilling forest music until thrilling boss battle themes. I really loved the music, it fit so well in every aspect and scene.
WARNING MAY CONTAIN SPOILERS STARTING HERE
Story:
Little Girl finds a ring, gets the quest to save the elven race, enemies are vampires and one plot twist after another. The beginning was sold so well, as the story advanced it kept me further going. I really didn't want to stop playing this game or try to play another one in between. Finished the game in one go with sleeping to the next day included. I wish the story could have had more content, but I'm satisfied how it is. I assume there won't be a sequel, so I'm not treating this ending as a potential cliffhanger. It's an open end and many things are still unsolved like why did Baramon even create vampires, why was Lita really chosen and succeeded (even many before tried to lift the curse and failed). My theory is still that she has the inner goddess inside her, but that's just my conspiracy. Why was Ara Fell even in the Sky? (laughed at the pun when Ara litereally Fell)
Characters & Design:
When I saw all the characters, which would have been in my party I just thought "urgh, I don't like them except Lita." In the end I loved them all. There is so much character development in each of them and I definitely have to say that Doren is my favourite character. It felt like he was the main character, because he saw the beginning and witnessed it to the end. At first I thought he is just a random bard in Lita's town, screw me. Totally laughed at all his ex-girl friends. Seri Kesu must felt so betrayed by him. Unlike Seri Kesu and Lita, Adrian felt really poor like he doesn't fit much as a main character in my opinion. The interaction between the characters, mostly between Adrian and Lita (awesome portraits sometimes) were hilarious, made me smile really often even in dangerous situations in the story. Design of the World was beautiful. The map in the beginning so confusing, but after crossing almost every map like 20 times, it came pretty handy.
SPOILER END
Gameplay   9.5/10
Music    10/10
Story    9/10
Characters & Design  9.5/10
Overall 9.5/10
To Sum up, it is the best RPGMaker 2k3 game I've played since Vampires Dawn 2 and i played many RPG2k3 games in the past and would definitely recommend it to people who are looking for a good 2k3 Maker game.
The chance is slim that there might be a sequel, however I hope one day there will be one, because the ending is a real big cliffhanger or you can make a prequel, to answer all those remaining questions. I would definitely put out my wallet and gladly pay 30€ or more for a 2nd part, aslong it has more than 20 hours gameplay and all the mechanics and features from the first game.

Rainbow Six Siege is a type of game that relies on your knowledge more than reaction and aiming as this game is a thinking man's game. When i first heard about this game i thought it looked incredible. Seeing gameplay on youtube of the intensity of close quarters firefights, splitsecond decisions that can make or break your game, and absolutely flawless teamwork that i could only dream of coming close to achieving. Seeing all of this i just had to have the game. I had a look on Steam to see how much it would cost me, and while having a look at the price of what i thought at the time would be a masterpiece i noticed something. This game was developed by Ubisoft. Now if you're unfamiliar with Ubisoft and their "mixed" history in making games, then allow me to explain to the best of my knowledge how they've been in recent years. Ubisoft is responsible for (in my personal opinion) many amazing games. They've released absolute gems like Assassin's Creed 2 and Far Cry 3, which captivated me and kept me on the edge of my seat. A few years ago if you asked me what i like about these games from Ubisoft i would be able to give you many reasons for why i love them. However now if you ask me why i liked them i can give a very simple reason, those games worked. In recent years Ubisoft's games are not being released as finished products. Many complain of Ubisoft introducing microtransactions into their games, gameplay being unoriginal or too simple, but most of the complaints are of the game just being broken. Playing Assassin's Creed Unity on PS4 i hadn't experienced many game breaking bugs, although the game was incredibly simple and got very boring very quickly. It wasn't until i purchased Assassin's Creed Rogue on PC that i truly understood the people's complaints. Simply put the game would just crash as soon as i would jump off the tree which my character starts in. I'd had enough, i told myself that Ubisoft had enough of my money already. Even when they we're initially releasing Rainbow Six Siege back in 2015 i told myself that i wasn't buying it, i was done with Ubisoft. When the game came out i saw i was right, much like some of their previous games Siege had been downgraded from what Ubisoft's initial game footage showed. After seeing this and being glad that i had kept my wallet in my pocket i moved on with my life. It wasn't until early 2017 that me and my friends had discussed getting the game. Since its release back in late 2015 Ubisoft had made a lot of changes, i figured that i would finally give it a chance. I went ahead and bought it.
So i got the game in about April of 2017 with my friends. They'd been watching many youtubers playing it and suggested that we get it. I'm going to give Ubisoft credit and say that they had made vast improvements from what i'd seen in the past. I thought the game looked beautiful, and i'm glad to say that for the first few months we played this game we had a blast. We had a tremendous amount of fun trying to play tactifully and having it pay off pretty well sometimes. It was a glorious time we had, but it didn't last much longer sadly. Looking into when Ubisoft would be releasing their next set of operators i came across a piece of news which reported that Ubisoft was delaying the new operators while they worked on maintenance for the game. I figured that it was probably for the best, there were bugs in the game of course but i was having so much fun that i ignored most of them. Ubisoft was titling this update "Operation Health". Ubisoft's first mistake with this update was missing the oportunity to call it "Operation Hemorrhoids", because this update was the biggest ♥♥♥♥ing pain in the♥♥♥♥♥i have ever experienced. For Ubisoft this update was 1 step forward and 2 MASSIVE steps back. The amount of new glitches i had experienced from this update was unreal. Getting the macthmaking to work was a hell of a task on it's own, but once i made it into the game i would find problems left and right. The hitboxes for the operators were a complete mess. I don't care how♥♥♥♥♥♥♥Fuze is, a headshot is a headshot and five bullets in his massive head should be complete overkill. But no don't worry fuze, Operation Health is here to save you. He gets a nice clean headshot on me while walking away only losing 30hp from the magazine i unloaded into his forehead. And to me that was it, i'd had enough. Until ubisoft fixed their mess i wasn't coming back. I took about a month off before i came back because i missed it. A few issues had been fixed, some characters nerfed and i was back to trying to have fun. Now we're in October , the new operators have been released, Operation Hemorrhoids is gone from my main menu and replaced with Operation Blood Orchid. So you're probably wondering if the game is now fixed right? I would say that it's not as bad as Operation Health, and some issues have been fixed. You're not going to find a perfect game here though, not yet at least. I'm going to continue playing the game because i do still have fun with it. You will find plenty of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t moments where the hitbox really isn't on your side, and you're thrown in matchmaking with a few coppers and a maybe a gold on your team, while the enemy team gets a diamond ranked ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and some platnum bros. But i stick with it for those amazing moments that come every so often, where you're the last man standing against the enemy team and you think to yourself "I'm gonna die or i'm gonna kill every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in that damn house, let's ♥♥♥♥ing go!" If you're not too sure about wether or not you'll like the game, just get the starter edition. You only start with 2 operators but i will give you a good look at the game without having to spend a lot of money on it. I'm gonna go ahead and recommend this game. Despite the overall tone of my review and my attitude towards Ubisoft, i really like this game and it still has plenty of potential if Ubisoft can just pull their thumb out of their♥♥♥♥♥ Take what you can from my experience and decide for yourself, i can more or less guarantee there is another "Operation Go ♥♥♥♥ Yourself" on the horizon though. If you want to be there to witness the absolute ♥♥♥♥♥how then go buy the game.

HOW TO FIX THE ISSUE WITH THE GAME NOT STARTING:
1. Locate Sacred2.exe in your Sacred 2 folder. In my case it's here: E:\Steam\steamapps\common\Sacred 2 Gold\system
2. Right click Sacred2.exe and click 'Properties'.
3. Click on the 'Compatibility' tab.
4. Enable Compatibility Mode, and run it for Windows XP SP3, push apply.
5. Launch Sacred2.exe as administrator.
6. Exit the game after launch.
7. Disable compatibility mode and click apply.
8. Everything should be working properly and you can now launch the game through Steam.

The original Sacred had some cool ideas and characters, though it was a bit rough around the edges. I never finished it, but I definitely respected certain things about it, even if I never could fully get behind it. Sacred 2, however, I'm even less lenient with. Sacred felt like a developer trying out some new things and trying to make an action RPG, with certain successes, and certain awkward things that don't really work well. In Sacred 2, however, I didn't feel like anything that didn't work well, such as the overall gameplay in general, and the orgy of different stats/skills to upgrade which were excessive in the first game already, make a shameless return to the sequel.
Quests are in no short supply, but no quests feel meaningful and I didn't really want to do them. Less is more in this situation. Loot was about the same as the first game, from what I noticed, which was pretty decent, and I like the fonts used in the game.
I had hoped for this to be a polished, better Sacred, but I didn't feel like that was what the product ended up as. There's no shame in being a Diablo clone if the setting, graphics, and gameplay feels good. Trying to be very different from it in feel, to the extent of feeling "really off," which is how the Sacred games made me feel, is not a step in the right direction.

This is one of those games that is appealing on so many levels. For start, i immediately noticed that the game is designed beautifully, from world to creatures, and ofcourse, the main character which really looks like the embodyment of war, wielding the biggest, and the most badass sword since Buster Sword. Story is very well written and actors did an amazing job voicing those cut scenes followed by memorable soundtrack. As for the gameplay, being the most important aspect of video games in my oppinion, i would say that the developers nailed it.
I have heard people comparing Darksiders with Zelda games and i would say they are right, cause Darksiders is one of those multy gameplay aspect games. You will be doing everything from world exploring, treasure hunting, money farming, puzzle solving, character upgrading and battling all kinds of enemies in this game.
Exploration is fun and very enjoyable because of the above mentioned beutifully designed world and many secrets that it hides.  Often you will come across new tools that will allow you to revisit all those places you have been at before but now you would be able to reach all those previously inaccessible spots and claim their treasures.
Combat is great, and i loved the fact that every enemy is challenging in its own way and that you can easily get outnumbered and usually killed if you dont use all the tools and moves that are at your disposal. Its fairly simple but at the same time, requires concentration and awareness. You will want to learn your enemies moves and try to counter them when they make an opening or by executing a perfect parry which will usually devastate them. Sadly, this game has a reverse difficulty curve, meaning that it will be hardest at the start and in time, combat will become much less challenging as u grow in power. However, boss fights are amazing! They are a perfect blend of combat skills and puzzle, and you can always count on these to provide a fair challenge.
Also, you should know that this game is not very well ported for PC. Expect FPS drops in some areas(the Ashlands for me) and even game crashing, which, to be honest, happened to me only once, when i first ran the game and met Vulgrim. You probably wont be able to use controller unless u have original XBOX controller(my PS2 controller would make the game unplayable by fixing the camera at awkward angle simply by being plugged in), and no, x360ce probably wont work for you, so you are stuck with a keayboard and mouse. Another very annoying thing are steam achievements which you will not be able to get unless you are running the game for the first time. Every time you quit and re-run Darksiders, you wont be able to achieve anything. Luckily, this is fixed in seconds by simply quitting steam and re-starting it again but you will have to do it every time you wanna play this game.
I usually try to go in details with my reviews but, to be honest, that would be it. Game has a simple concept, A to B route, filled with battle encounters, secrets and occasional puzzles(which are also simple but fun), and its executed perfectly. If you take these bad PC porting flaws out of the picture, Darksiders is an amazing game and likely one that you will remember and recommend

Darksiders, for the uninitiated, is a hack-and-slash game, similar to these in tis' calibre such as Devil May Cry series. In this title, you'll control War, one of the horseman, as a playable character. You can upgrade his abilities, weapons and durability as the gameplay progresses, by purchasing them from Vulgrim, and interactions with other characters such as Samael (Shadow Flight and Chronomancer), and the gate keepers (Shadow realm vision), etc.
The action and gameplay are above average for a hack and slash title. However, one of the things you'll appreciate about this game is that there are no freebies: Its' tough and challenging, and both mini-bosses and bosses are no exception. Even on easy, prepare to replay scenes as you battle the main bosses (Notably Tiamat and Silitha, two of the chosen).
Visuals: Okay. Scales well even on older hardware with reduced settings. Nothing spectacular here.
Game length: Satisfactory.
Caveat: The Horseman's steed, Ruin, is acquired much later in the game, and you need him to access some areas in the game. This also compounds into a second problem: Repeatability. You'll find yourself repeating sections later on as you acquire new abilities. This is a tolerable compromise, since the game length does not pack inconvenience in the process (Remember Skyrim? None of that time-packing and stretching is preent ).
All in all, it was a great primer to get started on as a game, and its' decent.
Overall rating: 8.7/10

So, I've played some games before that try to hold your hand a bit too much and may sin on having too many or too detailed tutorials, but I've never felt trated like a kid with Down's before like I do while playing Ara Fell.
Every little thing, every little detailed is explained in-game with a reading tutorial. The game alerts you to save everyy time something is about to happen, it even asks you if you want to continue forward twice every time.
I've only fought the first boss (the guy who kidnaps the villagers' pets) and here's how it went:
"Hey, you're about to enter a tough battle, do you want to save?"
"You need to have at least this level, this equipment, and this many people, okay?"
"Do you want to proceed?"
"Are you sure?"
"Look, in your first turn I'm giving you all the boss stats and his skills just so you know beforehand"
"And hey, let me take a moment to explain his special ability in detail"
"Just in case you didn't hear it first, everything will be repeated by the boss himself."
"But it's okay!" You can prevent it by attacking his minions!"
"Now, attack that one. Let me put a mark on him AND change his name to Chosen so you are 100% sure you got it"
"You still won't have time to kill it, though"
"That's okay, you can still kill the guy no probs."
Even if this was the first time I played an RPG, this would still be insulting my intelligence. Seriously, I have great expectation in this game but I can't keep playing something that treats me like an idiot at every opportunity given.
If you are okay with this, go on and play it, as I'm sure it has lots of redeeming qualities to it, but for me that's a big no-no.

Defintaley NOT Sid Meiers Antietam or Gettysburg.  The unit cohesion is very similar as well as the over all appearance, but all similarities stop there.
First there is no regimental command level.  You can not break up a brigade to send out a regiment of skirmishers.  which leads me to my second dissapointment.
There is no way to change a units formation.  You can not put a unit into column, skirmishers, or refuse a line.  There are "skirmishers" within the game but they are stuck as such.
What good are cavalry?  I understand the over all lack of fighting ability of cavalry against infantry, but seriously, some skirmishing power would be nice.  Also, if cavalry runs down a battery of guns guess who ends up running.  You certainly can not capture them.
I am also not sure what the metrics are for flanking.  I had an enemy bridage flanked and fought them off when they charged yet they continued to hang around and be a nuisance when they should have been completely routed.  I know the rout is possible because I have had some of my own brigades break.
Over all if you are looking for the second coming of the classic Sid Meiers then this is not it.  While it is 10x closer than the joke "Total War" series, it is to simple to be considered a serious replacement.  I might recommend it for $5, but not $15
